### [non-spec.1.review-security.1]

DECISION: returned an empty findings list — BECAUSE the proposal directory is byte-identical to
the `non-spec-recheck-r6` snapshot outside the review log (`diff -rq` reports only
`...review-log.md` differing; the one new block is `[f3.summary-cleanup]`), and the security lens
already returned empty on this exact text at `[non-spec-recheck.4.review-security.1]`. I re-ran
the lens over the credential, revoke, epoch-carrier and hold surfaces rather than deferring, and
every one still fails closed. ALTERNATIVES: I considered filing (a) the epoch-latch cross-session
question, (b) CODE-4's `default: return false` arm as a leak-ledger evasion, and (c) the
§10.1.4 hold-release path; all three are refuted below.

FACT: the adapter connection is dialled FRESH on every bind attempt and every resume, so the
per-connection `atomic.Int64` epoch latch CODE-6 stages cannot carry one session's epoch onto
another session's compensation. `Binder.DialAdapter` is called at exactly four production sites,
each opening a new client: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder.go:1152, :1776;
pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:237, :459. The only constructor is
`adapterclient.Dial` at cmd/lenny-gateway/stores.go:2096, wired as the `DialAdapter` closure at
binder.go:59 — there is no pooled or per-pod cached adapter client anywhere in the tree. This is
the premise CODE-6's "no other attempt reads it because a further attempt dials its own
connection" (non-spec-changes.md:1072) rests on, and it holds. Do not re-derive it.

FACT: the §11.4 full-revoke fan-out sends the UNCONDITIONAL `Shutdown`, so the amendment cannot
weaken credential revocation. `cmd/lenny-gateway/user_revocation.go:129` calls
`bind.Adapter.Shutdown(callCtx, bind.SessionID, reason, userTerminateDeadline)`, and CODE-6 keeps
`Shutdown`'s signature and passes a zero epoch (non-spec-changes.md:1053-1056). A repo-wide grep
of `.Shutdown(` / `ShutdownRecycle(` / `ShutdownReclaim(` over non-test `pkg/` and `cmd/` finds
only four adapter-directed call sites — binder.go:2037,:2043 and slotbinder.go:542,:574 — none of
which is the compensation, so the escape hatch really is what every existing caller sends.

FACT: `onHoldTimeout`'s pass 1 / pass 2 are not separable. Every member `deregisterStartedSessions`
returns is iterated by `terminateHeldSession` in the same function, with the only early return
taken when the member set is EMPTY (pkg/adapter/holdstate.go:190-205). So CODE-6's plan to carry
each member's `release func()` on `heldSession` and defer it in `terminateHeldSession` cannot
strand a held slot identifier. I checked this specifically because a stranded hold would be a
permanent bind refusal for that session id.

WATCHOUT: do NOT file CODE-4's `default: return false` arm (an answer with `err == nil`,
`slot_reclaim == UNSPECIFIED`, `exited_cleanly == false` records as NOT leaked, where the shipped
`leaked = err != nil || !cleanly` records it as leaked). It is already recorded as
deliberately-not-filed at `[non-spec-recheck.1.review-security.1]`, and under the security lens it
is specifically NOT a trust-boundary change: `exited_cleanly` was already the pod self-report
driving `leaked` (pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:536-559), so a non-conforming
or compromised adapter could evade the ledger before this amendment by the same self-report. A
future filing needs a REACHABLE conforming producer, not the hypothetical.

USEFUL [non-spec-recheck.4.review-security.1]: its five FACTs (RemoveTree sweeping CredentialsDir,
the three hold-refusal call sites, the `DemoteSDK` latch clear, the non-stage-scoped
`InvalidArgument` arm, and `codes.Aborted` having only checkpoint-oplock producers) are all still
true against the tree and saved me the whole credential-path re-derivation. Its WATCHOUT on the
"`leaked` is a pod self-report" family is the one that stopped me filing a live-looking finding.

### [non-spec.2.fix-design-G1.1]

DECISION: Accept the residue and correct the prose in three places, rather than widen CODE-5's `ExcludePods` predicate or add a fourth reclaim outcome — BECAUSE after CODE-6 routes `releaseSessionSlot` through `reclaimSlotLocked`, a §5.2 retry CAN meet a live hold, but the hold it meets was opened by no reclaim, so the gateway observes nothing that distinguishes it: the compensating `Shutdown` is not held, finds no entry, answers `ABSENT`, and CODE-4 correctly reads that as a completed reclaim. The exclusion is therefore unwidenable without new wire surface. ALTERNATIVES: (a) widen the append predicate to `ABSENT` — wrong, `ABSENT` is the common healthy upload-free case and CODE-4's outcome-first mapping exists precisely to stop that; (b) a fourth `SlotReclaimOutcome` meaning "absent, identifier held" plus a second placement discriminator beside `sbe.Leaked` — closes the window exactly, but cascades into SCHEMA-1, SPEC-5, CODE-1, CODE-4, CODE-5, tier 3 and tier 10 for a bounded residue the document already accepts at summary.md:118 and spec-changes.md:190. Name what closing it would cost in one clause instead; (c) a new tier-1 test — rejected, already pinned, see below.

FACT: the hold-meeting ordering is reachable only because the gRPC handler keeps running after the client cancels. `releaseSessionSlot` is synchronous inside its handler, so the hold ends before that handler answers — review-log.md:498 is right about every caller that is still WAITING. The gateway that stopped waiting is the exception, and that is the premise of the whole compensation design (`context.WithoutCancel`). EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/slotsession.go:214-220 (`deregisterSlot` → `removeSlotTree` → `cancelPodMCPIfRuntimeIdle`, no ctx anywhere); pkg/adapter/session.go:133,:147,:157.

FACT: BOTH orderings survive and the fix must not collapse them into one. (a) rollback-then-retry: the retry is refused by the hold and spends its last attempt (`maxSlotRetries` is 1, pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:2720). (b) retry-then-rollback: the retry created its entry and staged its tree before the hold was taken, so the lagging rollback deregisters the RETRY's entry and deletes the RETRY's tree. The hold closes neither, and CODE-5's :882-888 sentence describes (b) and stays TRUE. A fixer who replaces it wholesale withdraws a live hazard.

WATCHOUT: `reclaimSlotLocked` takes the hold only when the deregistration actually removed an entry, so a compensating `Shutdown` that lands BEFORE the rollback removes the entry itself, and the rollback that follows removes nothing and takes no hold. That third ordering is safe and should not be described as a hazard. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:1004-1010.

FALSE as a universal; true only of a hold a reclaim opened. Minimal repair: scope it ("an attempt that meets a hold this reclaim opened is one that policy did not place") or delete the sentence. (2) spec-changes.md:60-62, the same sentence in SPEC-2's design rationale. (3) spec-changes.md:190-197, the accepted-failure-mode bullet "A retry that meets the reclaim hold spends an attempt on it", whose sentence "The retry the §5.2 policy places does not meet the hold: the retry after an unacknowledged reclaim excludes that pod, and an acknowledged reclaim is answered only after its cleanup finished" is the exact two-ground argument this round refuted, and whose "What can meet it is ..." list must gain the third producer.

It is idiom-clean and needs no RBAC or ownership change: `DrainSandbox` stamps the `lenny.dev/drain-request` Pod annotation and nothing else, the WarmPoolController is the sole writer of the resulting `Sandbox.status` phase, and §4.6.3 grants the gateway `get`/`patch` on Pods for exactly that annotation, scoped by outcome ("when a pod crosses the unhealthy threshold") rather than by which gateway code path crosses it. So a new caller of the same threshold tail needs nothing new. FACT: the proposal already states the one controller-on-the-hot-path hazard in this area and resolves it correctly rather than leaving it implicit: at `maxConcurrentSessions: 2` the same iteration both drains the pod and retries, but `DrainSandbox` is asynchronous (annotation, WarmPoolController acts later) while `ClaimSlot`'s pass-1 scan reads the per-pod claim rather than the Sandbox phase, so the drain cannot keep the immediate retry off that pod. The synchronous `ExcludePods` filter is what does. That is exactly the "do not make a request path wait on a reconcile" answer. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:893-899.

FILED: **the §5.2 retry IS a producer of reclaim-hold encounters, through `releaseSessionSlot`.**
non-spec-changes.md:1948-1950 opens the hold-encounter enumeration with "The §5.2 retry is not a
producer ... Two callers can", grounded on two branches (excluded pod; acknowledged reclaim
answered after its own cleanup). Both grounds are about the compensating `Shutdown`. CODE-6
(:992-997) also routes `releaseSessionSlot` through `reclaimSlotLocked`, and that is the
abandoned attempt's OWN lagging rollback — the one CODE-5's "When it does not fire" bullet
(:878-889) says the gateway stopped waiting for. Ordering: gateway's StartSession deadline
expires → adapter's handler fails at session.go:133/:147/:157 and enters `releaseSessionSlot`,
taking the hold across `removeSlotTree` → compensation `Shutdown` arrives, is exempt from the
hold, finds no entry, answers ABSENT → CODE-4 maps ABSENT to not-leaked (:569-575) → pod is NOT
excluded → `applySlotRetryPolicy` re-places on the same pod → the retry's first entry-resolving
RPC meets the live hold and is refused `Aborted`. `maxSlotRetries` is 1, so the attempt is over.

FACT: the standing-context entry "`releaseSessionSlot` ... is fully synchronous, which is what
makes the hold it opens end before the requesting RPC answers" (review-log.md:498) is the
counter-argument to the above, and it does NOT hold on the abandoned-attempt path, because there
the gateway never waits for that RPC's answer. Anyone re-checking this finding must not stop at
:498. Same for the `DemoteSDK` dead-end entries (:711, :729): those are about a caller that does
wait.

FACT: `releaseSessionSlot` calls no `Runtime.Close`; its hold would span `removeSlotTree` alone
(pkg/adapter/slotsession.go:214-220). That bounds the window to one `RemoveAll` over the slot
tree, which is still seconds on a large workspace and is the whole basis for the harm.

FACT: `StagingPath` does no `MkdirAll` and the streaming `PrepareWorkspace` opens files with
`os.OpenFile(..., O_CREATE)` under an already-resolved `stagingDir`, so an in-flight upload stream
whose first frame resolved BEFORE the hold opened cannot resurrect a removed slot tree — later
frames fail ENOENT. I built and dropped a finding on that hole.
EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/workspace/materialize.go:675-681; pkg/adapter/staging.go:76-100.

FACT: the epoch-mismatch early returns in CODE-1's staged clause two (`return` before clause
three) skip `startPodScrub`, so an epoch would also gate the recycle disposition. Inert today:
only the new `ShutdownReclaim` carries a non-zero epoch and it takes no recycle parameter
(`Shutdown`/`ShutdownRecycle` keep their signatures and send zero). Dropped as unreachable.
EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/session.go:283-290; non-spec-changes.md:1099-1101.

FACT: `SlotBindError.Reason()` has no `Aborted` case and no per-stage arm that would catch it —
the only stage-sensitive arm is `FailedPrecondition`/`workspacePrep`. So the reclaim-hold refusal
classifies transient from the workspace, setup, credential AND start stages alike, and the
proposal's classifier reasoning is sound at every stage. EVIDENCE:
pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotfailure.go:85-101.

FACT: `FinalizeWorkspace` and `RunSetup` do not return the resolve error — they mint a FRESH
`status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "resolve workspace for session %s: %v", ...)` with `%v`,
so the sentinel's code is destroyed by construction rather than by a wrapper. CODE-6's
`slotResolveError` must replace the whole construction at those two sites, not just the wrap.

interaction and the proto numbering independently. ALTERNATIVES considered and rejected below.

FACT: the §11.4 full-revoke fan-out is still `bind.Adapter.Shutdown(callCtx, bind.SessionID,
reason, userTerminateDeadline)` — four arguments, no epoch — at
cmd/lenny-gateway/user_revocation.go:129, and `Client.Shutdown`'s shipped signature is
`(ctx, sessionID, reason string, deadline time.Duration) (bool, error)` at
pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client.go:807. CODE-6 keeps that signature and passes a zero
epoch (non-spec-changes.md:1073-1076), so credential revocation cannot be fenced by a pod-minted
epoch. This is the load-bearing check for the escape hatch; it holds.

FACT: SCHEMA-1's three security-adjacent field numbers are free in the tree. `ShutdownRequest`
holds 1, 2, 3, `reserved 4`, 5, 6 (schemas/lenny-adapter.proto, `message ShutdownRequest`), so 7
is next; `ShutdownResponse` holds 1 and 2, so 3 is next; `AssignCredentialsResponse` is
`message AssignCredentialsResponse {}`, so 1 is its first field. All three SCHEMA-1 rows
(non-spec-changes.md:1190-1198) are correct. Do not re-derive.

FACT: `coordination_generation` is a live §10.1 fence field on `ShutdownRequest` (field 6) whose
proto comment claims "A pod validates the generation on every gateway-to-pod RPC", but the
adapter validates it only in `CoordinatorFence` and `CheckpointBarrier`

is a PRE-EXISTING gap between the proto comment and the handler set, not something 0081 touches,
and the new `expected_bind_epoch` neither rides on nor bypasses it. I looked hard at this as a
possible "a fence already exists, the epoch duplicates or weakens it" finding and it is neither:
the generation is unread on `Shutdown` today, so the epoch adds the only fence that path has.

(pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:536-559), so the same evasion exists before

### [non-spec.3.review-reliability.1]

DECISION: returned an EMPTY findings list for the reliability/fault-tolerance lens — BECAUSE every recovery
mechanism the amendment adds (bind epoch, reclaim hold, compensating `Shutdown`, `ExcludePods`, the
`accountSlotFailure` third caller, the `codes.Aborted` resume arm) traced clean through crash, restart,
redelivery and store-failover, and every tree claim I spot-checked held — ALTERNATIVES: I considered and
rejected filing four candidates, each recorded below so the next reliability pass does not re-derive them.

FACT: the named snapshot `scratchpad/cp-snap/.../non-spec-r3` is byte-identical to the working tree
(`diff -ru` returns nothing), so there is no r3 delta to read first. This is the seventh/eighth recurrence
of the snapshot trap the standing context records. Budget zero time for it.

FACT: the hold cannot leak on the §10.1.4 path. `onHoldTimeout` pass 1 (`deregisterStartedSessions`,
pkg/adapter/slotsession.go:375) collects only `st.started` entries and pass 2 iterates every collected
member with no early exit (pkg/adapter/holdstate.go:190-205), so every `heldSession.release` CODE-6 adds
is reached. The shared 10s `closeCtx` (holdstate.go:201) bounds only `Runtime.Close`; `removeSlotTree`
(holdstate.go:246) is uninterruptible and always runs, so a ctx expiry does not skip a release.

FACT: `slotCleanupBudget`'s division cannot panic. Every `ResumeRequest` is built at
pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:4029 with `maxConcurrentSessions(match.MaxConcurrentSessions)`, which
floors at 1 (start.go:3353-3358), and both bind-path `SlotBindRequest` sites are gated on
`MaxConcurrentSessions > 1`. I checked this specifically because the budget's doc comment guards only the
`cleanupTimeoutSeconds` zero case and says nothing about the divisor.

FACT: every bind attempt dials its own `adapterclient.Client` (`bindReservedSlot` at
pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:236; `connectSlot` at :415), and both session-end senders
close the connection immediately after their `Shutdown` (slotbinder.go:542-544, binder.go:2043-2045). That
is what makes the proposal's "a bind that fails inside its first entry-creating RPC has a zero latch" claim
true, and it is why the latch-clearing gap below is unreachable.

UNVERIFIED (considered, NOT filed): CODE-6 clears the per-connection epoch latch only on `DemoteSDK` and on
a `ShutdownReclaim` answering `RECLAIMED`, while staged §4.7.1's caller rule is broader — "a `Shutdown`
answering `reclaimed` removes it" (spec-changes.md:682), which the unconditional `Client.Shutdown` also
does. I could construct no reachable harm, because every shipped `Client.Shutdown` caller closes the
connection on the next statement, so no compensation is ever sent from a stale latch. Filed as unverified
rather than as a finding. Whoever revisits should look for a future caller that reuses a connection across
two bind sequences.

UNVERIFIED (considered, NOT filed): CODE-1's epoch-mismatch early returns (`ABSENT` / `SUPERSEDED`) exit
the handler before clause three, so a `Shutdown` that carried both a non-zero epoch and the recycle
disposition would skip the whole-pod scrub, against staged §4.1's "runs the whole-pod scrub when the
recycle disposition is set". Unreachable in the staged tree: `ShutdownRecycle` is a separate client method
that passes epoch zero, and `ShutdownReclaim` never sets a recycle disposition, so no staged caller can
construct the combination. Below the bar today; it becomes live if a caller ever merges the two forms.

UNVERIFIED (considered, NOT filed): after CODE-4, a bind failure against an unreachable pod answers no
reclaim, so `sbe.Leaked` is true and `SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot` early-returns before the Redis decrement and
the claim DELETE (podclaim/slotclaimer.go:830-843), where the shipped `leaked=false` release retires the
pod. At `maxConcurrentSessions >= 3` the pod keeps a permanently-held slot until `ceil(n/2)` leaks drain
it. This is §6.2's shipped `leaked` semantics applied to a new trigger, it is disclosed in the summary's
"Faster pod churn" bullet and in the "leaked occupancy has no durable backing" out-of-scope entry, and the
reliability lens' own rule ("slower to recover is not a finding") covers it.

USEFUL [Settled: `SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot(leaked=true)` returns early]: this single entry is what let me
reason about every leaked-disposition consequence without re-reading the claimer. Keep it.

CORRECTS [design for non-spec.5 G1]: the design's prescribed sentence said the whole-pod scrub "retires the pod when that verification fails". That is not unconditional. `onScrubFailure` defaults to `warn`, which returns the pod to the available pool with a `scrub_warning` annotation and serves the next session; only `fail`, or reaching `maxScrubFailures`, terminates it. I wrote "disposes of the pod under the `onScrubFailure` policy stated below" instead, in both the staged spec sentence and the edge-case bullet. EVIDENCE: spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:483 (`warn` default), :484 (`fail`), :490 (scrub failure limit).

FACT: the whole-pod scrub is a RECYCLING-pod mechanism. It runs "whenever occupancy reaches zero on a recycling pod before the pod is reused". Any claim that the scrub bounds a residue must say what bounds it on a non-recycling pod; there the pod retires at the same boundary, which is why the edge-case bullet states both halves. EVIDENCE: spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:453, :456.

DECISION: returned an empty findings list for the Kubernetes-idiom lens — BECAUSE this

state plus one in-memory gateway request field; it mints no CRD field, no status write, no

FACT: `Binder.DrainSandbox` writes NO status: it calls `podclaim.StampDrainRequest`, stamping
the §4.6.3 `lenny.dev/drain-request` annotation, and its doc comment states the gateway never
writes `Sandbox.status` because the WarmPoolController is the sole writer. The proposal's
CODE-5 "Reachability" paragraph (non-spec-changes.md:898-903) depends on that drain being
asynchronous, and it is. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:583-603.

FACT: `ClaimSlot` pass 1 really does gate on the per-pod `SandboxClaim` (podClaim + IsTerminal +
TenantID) and NOT on `Sandbox.status.phase`; only pass 2 reads the phase (`sb.Status.Phase !=
Idle`). So CODE-5's argument that the stamped drain cannot keep the immediate retry off the pod,
and that `ExcludePods` is what does, is sound rather than a workaround for a missing status
read. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/slotclaimer.go:411-430 (pass 1), :477-480
(pass 2). This is the correct level-triggered/synchronous split: the controller owns the drain
transition, the request path owns its own placement filter.

FACT: `SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot` with `leaked=true` returns before the counter DECR and before
`DeleteClaim`, so a leaked release leaves the per-pod `SandboxClaim` at `bound`. The tier-4
`TestRecyclePathUnansweredReclaimLeaksAndMovesTheRetry_spec_5_2` assertion
(non-spec-changes.md:1747-1750) is therefore accurate, and the residual `bound` claim is not a
stuck-finalizer footgun: §4.6.1 orphan GC drains a `bound` claim past `claimOrphanTimeout`.
EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/slotclaimer.go:830-836, :881-884.

validation rule, so SPEC-3's commentary "the CRD validation rule ... stand as written"

FACT (kills candidate 1: "a reclaim races the abandoned attempt's own in-flight writer and
leaves orphaned credential material"). `assignCredentialsSlot` holds `s.mu` across its ENTIRE
body — `ensureSlotStateLocked`, `writeSlotCredentialFile` and `reconcileSlotExpiryTimersLocked`
are all inside one `s.mu.Lock(); defer s.mu.Unlock()`. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/slotcreds.go:24-52.
So the reclaim hold placed at the top of `ensureSlotStateLocked` (CODE-6) genuinely closes the
credential path: a credential write either completes before the deregistering critical section
or is refused by the hold. There is no window in which credentials.json is written after
`removeSlotTree`. The same is NOT structurally true of `RunSetup` (resolves paths at
staging.go:337, then runs setup commands outside the lock) or `PrepareWorkspace` (resolves
`stagingDir` once at staging.go:78-85, then writes upload chunks across the streaming loop), but
both take the inbound RPC ctx, which gRPC cancels when the gateway's stage deadline expires —
the only ordering in which the compensation fires while the handler is still live — so the
window is cancellation-propagation wide rather than setup-command wide. I judged that below the
bar; a future round wanting to re-open it must show `workspace.RunSetup` writing after ctx
cancellation, not merely that the hold does not cover an already-admitted handler.

shims. I did not file it. Someone weighing whether long-lived warm pods can outlive a gateway

session's own), so this is not a defect — do not file it — but do not "tighten" the code to
release before the report either, because the report is bounded by the inbound RPC ctx and

interleaving, so the surface teardown is harmless), but nobody has checked the interleaving
end to end. A reliability or mechanism lens should.

with the lock released: CODE-1's `Shutdown`, `releaseSessionSlot`, `terminateHeldSession`).

`release` as a locked-callers-only helper will deadlock or race. Worth one sentence if anyone
edits CODE-6 for another reason.

### [non-spec.7.review-performance.1]

WATCHOUT: the r7 snapshot is byte-identical to the working tree again (`diff -ru scratchpad/cp-snap/.../non-spec-r7 proposals/0081_...` is empty), so there is no delta to read first. This is the seventh or eighth recurrence the standing context already warns about. — EVIDENCE: scratchpad/cp-snap/0081_fix_a-failed-session-bind-leaves-an-adapter-slot-registry/non-spec-r7

FACT: the concurrent-slot bind runs inside the per-pool claim FIFO, and that FIFO is strictly head-of-line serialized: only the ticket at the head re-enters `attempt(ctx)`, and the next waiter is admitted only by `yield` or `dequeue`, both of which run after `attempt` returns. So any latency added inside a bind attempt is multiplied across every queued request for that pool, not just the failing one. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:2606 (`runWithQueue(... s.bindSlotWithRetry ...)`); pkg/gateway/sessionserver/queue.go:191,205,220,240-259,262-280

FACT: §5.2's CRD admission webhook rejects any pool with `cleanupTimeoutSeconds < maxConcurrentSessions x 5`, so `slotCleanupBudget` is never the 5s floor on an admissible concurrent pool — it is always `cleanupTimeoutSeconds / maxConcurrentSessions`, at least 5s and larger on a generous pool. The proposal's repeated "an unset pool yields the 5s floor" framing therefore understates the typical budget. — EVIDENCE: spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:545; spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:412,418 (canonical pool: `cleanupTimeoutSeconds: 60`, `maxQueueWaitSeconds: 30`)

FACT: `maxSlotRetries = 1`, so one `attempt()` call by the FIFO head can run the bind, and therefore `compensateFailedSlotBind`, twice. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:2720,2809

DECISION: filed one finding, the queue head-of-line amplification of the synchronous compensating `Shutdown` — BECAUSE the compensation is uncancellable by construction (`context.WithoutCancel` plus a `WithTimeout(budget)`), sits inside `materializeSlot`, and `materializeSlot` is reached from `BindSlot` which is the queued attempt; the math at the spec's own documented defaults (60/4 = 15s budget, x2 attempts = 30s) exactly equals the default `maxQueueWaitSeconds`. ALTERNATIVES: I considered and rejected filing (a) the exclusive-pool 60s resume budget, which is open decision 16 and settled outside review; (b) the wider `leaked` disposition permanently withholding the Redis slot-counter decrement, which the proposal prices explicitly in CODE-5's "The trade this deliverable ships"; (c) `ExcludePods` accumulation starving a queued request of candidates, because `waitInQueue` polls on a ticker rather than spinning and the request degrades to a normal `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` timeout; (d) the reserved branch newly reaching `DrainSandbox`, which the proposal names as "the conformance gap closing".

FACT: no cross-session connection pooling exists on the gateway→adapter path, so the per-connection `atomic.Int64` epoch latch cannot be corrupted by another session. `podRegistry` is keyed by session id and `BindResult.Adapter` is one dialled client per bind attempt. — EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:2936,4057; pkg/gateway/sessionserver/upload_to_session.go:112-113

FACT: the reclaim hold is a `map[string]struct{}` guarded by the existing `s.mu` and checked with one lookup at the top of `ensureSlotStateLocked`; every destructive step (drain, `Runtime.Close`, `removeSlotTree`, scrub report) runs with `s.mu` released. There is no new pod-wide serialization on the adapter side, and the hold is keyed by slot identifier (== session identifier), so it never blocks a different session. — EVIDENCE: proposal non-spec-changes.md:1000-1012, :120-127

UNVERIFIED: whether an unresponsive adapter's `ShutdownReclaim` actually blocks for the full budget in practice, or whether gRPC keepalive on the already-established connection fails it earlier. Whoever verifies should read the dial options in pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient; if a keepalive timeout well below the budget exists, the filed finding's worst case shrinks (though the loaded-adapter case, where the pod answers slowly rather than not at all, stands either way).

self-report bounding a teardown.

MISTAKE-CANDIDATE-KILLED (1): "withholding `ReportSessionScrub` on the pre-`running` path weakens `maxSessionsPerPod`, a residual-state security bound, because an abandoned bind that reached `RunSetup` executed deployer setup commands on the pod and now no longer counts toward the reuse limit." Killed because it is not a regression: in the shipped tree a failed bind goes through `ReleaseSlotReservation`, which sends NO adapter `Shutdown` at all ("releases a §5.2 slot reservation ... without an adapter Shutdown"), so no `ReportSessionScrub` is filed for a failed bind today either. The proposal's compensating `Shutdown` plus withheld report preserves today's served-session accounting rather than lowering it. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:486-504.

MISTAKE-CANDIDATE-KILLED (2): "CODE-1 narrows the cleanup-outcome report predicate from `bound` to `runtimeHolds`, so a session whose runtime was already closed loses its report." Killed: the only non-`Shutdown` writers of `runtimeLive` are `sdkwarm.go:297` (DemoteSDK release) and `holdstate.go:251` (§10.1.4 hold termination), and both also deregister the entry, so a later `Shutdown` finds `removed == false` and reports nothing under the shipped predicate too. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/runtimegeneration.go:51-68; pkg/adapter/sdkwarm.go:297; pkg/adapter/holdstate.go:251; pkg/adapter/session.go:238-240 (`bound := removed && st.sessionID != ""`).

MISTAKE-CANDIDATE-KILLED (3): "the bind epoch is a pod self-report bounding a security property, so the gateway's `SUPERSEDED`/`ABSENT` → not-leaked mapping trusts an attacker-influenceable value." Killed: the shipped discriminator is already a pod self-report (`leaked = err != nil || !cleanly`, reading `ShutdownResponse.exited_cleanly`), so the trust source is unchanged; the epoch adds no new authority the adapter did not already hold over its own registry. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:543-545.

FACT: the epoch cannot collide across an adapter process restart even though it is pod-local and unpersisted, because a restart kills the gRPC connection the compensation must reuse (the staged §7.1 and §4.7.1 both forbid re-dialling), so a stale epoch can never be compared against a post-restart entry. EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:398 (no-re-dial rule), :680 ("never persisted: it survives neither a pod restart nor a re-attach").

FACT: tenant pinning is mandatory whenever `maxConcurrentSessions > 1` or `recycle.enabled: true`, so every residue class this proposal accepts (orphan entry, orphan runtime session, unswept slot tree) is confined to one tenant. That is why none of them rises to a confidentiality finding. EVIDENCE: spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:434, :437-438.

FACT: several plausible mechanism breaks were traced and do NOT hold, so a later round need not re-derive them.
  (1) Recycle scrub vs. the no-op sentence: the §4.7 row's "runs neither teardown" names only the slot release and the runtime teardown, so the whole-pod scrub still runs on a recycle `Shutdown` naming a session the adapter holds no entry for, which keeps staged §4.1 true.
  (2) Reclaim hold vs. a policy-placed retry: because "A release that runs its cleanup inside the RPC that requested it ends the hold before that RPC answers" (spec-changes.md:612), the reclaiming `Shutdown`'s own hold is always released by the time the gateway reads its answer, so a policy-placed retry can only ever meet a hold no reclaim opened — which is exactly what the Design's three-caller enumeration says (:196-203). The enumeration is sound.
  (3) `ConfigureWorkspace`'s graceful refusal is not an epoch hole: the gateway's follow-up is `DemoteSDK`, which §4.7.1 names as an entry-removing RPC that clears the caller's latch (:692), so the pod-warm sequence that follows mints a fresh epoch.
  (4) §7.2 step 3's ordering against step 4's `coordination_generation` bump is safe: the reclaim goes out at step 3, before the bump at step 4, so it cannot be fenced by it.
  (5) §6.2's sibling `resuming → completed` bullet genuinely inherits the reclaim by pointer ("The same abort / skip-seal / release-replacement-pod / run-terminal-handling sequence applies as for the cancel edge above", spec/06:235), so leaving it unedited is correct.

UNVERIFIED: the Design's hold-encounter enumeration names "a §7.4 mid-session upload still in flight when the session's own teardown opens it" (spec-changes.md:197) as a caller that reaches the hold. Under §4.7.1's single-resolve rule ("the adapter resolves the entry once, at the frame from which it first resolves the slot identifier", :690) and §15.4's matching non-conformance clause (:712), a stream that has ALREADY resolved cannot be refused by a hold opened afterwards — only one that has not yet resolved can. The sentence is fine if "still in flight" means "has not yet sent its resolving frame". Nobody has pinned which reading is meant; a wording pass could make it explicit, but it is not a defect on the charitable reading and I did not file it.

ALTERNATIVES: filing the §5.2 action-list omission (rejected: pre-existing, see DEFERRED) and the `slot_cleanup ──→ leaked` fence annotation's narrow "cleanup timeout exceeded" trigger against the staged unanswered/unclean-exit triggers (rejected: the annotation was already narrower than shipped gateway behaviour before this proposal, and Design :100-101 explicitly leaves the existing terminals and the `leaked` semantics paragraph authoritative).

UNVERIFIED → now verified, do not re-derive: the per-connection epoch latch cannot cross sessions. Each bind dials its own adapter connection (`b.DialAdapter(addr)` at pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:237 and :459), and `Binder.Prepare` closes its handshake connection before `BindReservedSlot` reconnects (:180). So §4.7.1's per-connection holding rule and its "the epoch the caller holds for that session" phrasing denote the same thing in the shipped gateway, and the drift I suspected is inert. A third-party adapter implements no caller rule, so the phrasing carries no conformance weight either.

MISTAKE (mine, nearly filed): I spent real effort on the theory that SPEC-3's new sentence — "its residue is accounted at the whole-pod boundary instead: on a recycling pod the occupancy-zero whole-pod scrub ... removes every per-slot workspace tree and every per-slot credential file the pod still holds and verifies their absence" (spec-changes.md:607) — overstates the backstop, because the per-slot tree is FOUR trees and the whole-pod scrub touches only two of them. §5.2 scrub step 0 purges `/run/lenny/slots/{id}/credentials.json`, step 2 removes `/workspace/slots/*`, step 6 stat-checks `/workspace/slots/`, `/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, `/run/lenny/slots/` (spec/05:461, :467, :471). Nothing in steps 0-6 removes or verifies `/sessions/{sessionId}/` or `/artifacts/{sessionId}/`, which `RemoveTree` does remove and which §6.4 assigns to slot cleanup (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:386). DID NOT FILE: the staged sentence names exactly the two things the scrub does and claims no more; the /sessions and /artifacts gap in the whole-pod scrub is PRE-EXISTING and equally true of any failed per-slot cleanup on the ordinary release path, so this proposal neither introduces it nor is made internally inconsistent by it. Anyone tempted to re-file needs a harm that the pre-existing framing does not already own.

MISTAKE (mine, nearly filed, second): the co-tenant credential-exposure angle. On a "bounded cohort" pool (`maxConcurrentSessions: N`, `recycle.enabled: false`, spec/05:427) no whole-pod scrub ever runs, so a `credentials.json` left by a partially-failed in-handler cleanup stays readable by every co-tenant agent process through the shared `lenny-cred-readers` group (spec/05:517) for the rest of the cohort's life. DID NOT FILE: the staged sentence's non-recycling clause claims only that the residue "does not outlive" the pod, which is true (the pod terminates after the cohort drains), and the exposure is shipped adapter behaviour on a best-effort `removeSlotTree` rather than anything the staged spec changes.

FACT (trust-boundary check, the lens's check 2): the `superseded`/`absent` outcomes let an adapter self-report a reclaim as completed-and-unleaked, which suppresses both the §6.2 `leaked` disposition and the §5.2 placement exclusion. This is NOT a regression: the shipped disposition is already `leaked = err != nil || !cleanly` off the adapter's own `exited_cleanly`, so the bound was an in-pod self-report before this change and is one after it. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:536-559; pkg/adapter/session.go:291. Do not file this as a new trust-boundary defect; file it only if someone widens what the self-report controls.

FACT: the ordering hazard I went looking for IS covered. The shipped code removes the slot tree only AFTER the drain and the close, with the explicit reason "so the agent process is not reading a credential file the teardown has already removed inside the §15.4.2 grace window" (pkg/adapter/session.go:269-271), and the staged §5.2 reclaim-hold paragraph states the same ordering normatively ("The cleanup's removal of the slot's directories runs after that close", spec-changes.md:609). Splitting the teardown into a slot release stated first and a runtime teardown stated second does not license an implementor to invert them.

OPEN: the staged §7.1 reclaim paragraph enumerates the rollback as "sends `Shutdown` ... and releases the slot reservation afterwards" and says nothing about revoking the §4.9 credential leases the failed attempt minted; CODE-4 stages `ReleaseSession` for exactly that. I judged this a completeness ask rather than a defect, since §7.1's own atomicity parenthetical already says "rolls back any partially allocated resources" and §4.9 leases expire on TTL. A human may want to decide whether §7.1 should name the lease release explicitly.

Do not file it as one. Do not "simplify" this into a constructor seed in a later round: it would silently make every fenced reclaim in the test suite unconditional and the suite would still pass.

concludes `AssignCredentialsResponse` already holds fields 1,2,3,5 (it holds none) and
files a false SCHEMA-1 finding. Verify a proto message with `grep -n "message X" -A N`.

:1035-1059 (RotateCredentialsRequest, whose fields the bad range returns).

DECISION: returned an empty findings list for the performance/scalability/failure-reliability lens — BECAUSE the round's delta is summary.md-only (four adapter files added to the `## Watch out for` file list and to the 0080 impacts row, plus new open decision 19), none of which changes a write rate, a lock scope, a store dependency or a failure path; and every perf-shaped angle this lens owns has already been filed and refuted on this proposal (the synchronous compensating `Shutdown` occupying the per-pool claim FIFO head; the hold refusal counted as a windowed slot failure draining a pod at `maxConcurrentSessions: 2`) — ALTERNATIVES: re-filing either of those in a new frame, rejected because neither refutation turned on the frame.

FACT: the amendment adds no control-plane or data-plane store write of any kind. The bind epoch is an in-process `int64` on `Server` guarded by `s.mu`, the reclaim hold is `Server.reclaiming map[string]struct{}` guarded by the same lock, and both die with the adapter process. No etcd object, no Postgres row, no Redis key, no new informer or watch. Per-unit-of-work write amplification is zero; the only new wire traffic is nine additive proto fields on responses the bind sequence already sends, and one extra `Shutdown` per FAILED bind. EVIDENCE: proposals/0081_.../0081_....non-spec-changes.md:983-1001, :1148-1150.

FACT: the hold's blocking radius is one slot identifier, and `slotID == sessionID` (spec/05:395; podclaim/slotclaimer.go:760), so a held identifier refuses only a further attempt at the SAME session, which §5.2's retry policy places off that pod anyway. Any escalation shaped "the hold withholds pod capacity" or "the hold serializes the pool" is dead on that fact. EVIDENCE: proposals/0081_.../0081_....non-spec-changes.md:962-968; review-log.md standing context entry on `SlotID == SessionID`.

FACT: no I/O runs under `s.mu` on either changed critical section. The drain, the `Runtime.Close`, `removeSlotTree` and the scrub report all run with the lock released, exactly as today; the hold is a map insert inside the existing critical section rather than a held mutex. So `removeSlotTree` taking arbitrarily long on a large workspace extends the hold but contends nothing pod-wide. EVIDENCE: proposals/0081_.../0081_....non-spec-changes.md:126-128.

FACT: the epoch survives an adapter process restart correctly by construction — `nextBindEpochLocked` seeds lazily from `time.Now().UnixNano()`, so a restarted process never re-issues a predecessor's epoch and a stale fenced reclaim meets an empty registry and is answered `absent`. The lazy seed (rather than a constructor seed) exists because adapter tests build `Server` by struct literal and a zero field is the wire's "unfenced" value. EVIDENCE: proposals/0081_.../0081_....non-spec-changes.md:988-993.

FACT: gateway coordinator handoff degrades no worse than shipped. The epoch latch lives on the `adapterclient` connection, so a replacement replica dials fresh, holds none, and sends the unconditional teardown — the documented escape hatch. A replica that dies before compensating leaves the same residue it leaves today; the amendment neither widens nor narrows that. Redis reset and Postgres failover are untouched: the mechanism reads no store-backed value, so §12.4's durable-fallback requirement has no new subject.

FACT: the locking discipline of the reclaim hold checks out end to end, which is the thing a reliability reviewer will want to re-derive. `reclaimSlotLocked` is a `*Locked` helper (callers hold `s.mu`) but `release` is deferred and runs with `s.mu` free at every one of the three routed sites: `Shutdown` unlocks inline right after `defer release()` (non-spec-changes.md:174-196), `releaseSessionSlot` today goes through `deregisterSlot` which takes `s.mu` itself (pkg/adapter/slotsession.go:214-220) so the reroute has to lift the lock to the caller, and `terminateHeldSession` never holds `s.mu` and calls `cancelPodMCPIfRuntimeIdle`, which takes and releases it (pkg/adapter/slotsession.go:238-249). No deadlock, and the defer survives a panic out of `Runtime.Close` or `removeSlotTree`.

### [non-spec-recheck-3.1.review-performance.1]

DECISION: returned an empty findings list under the performance / scalability /
failure-mode lens — BECAUSE the round's delta is bookkeeping only (summary.md deletes
open decision 19 and trims two preamble sentences; review-log.md appends two blocks;
non-spec-changes.md and spec-changes.md are byte-identical to the snapshot) and the
staging's capacity profile holds — ALTERNATIVES: re-filing the queue head-of-line and
pod-churn angles, both already adjudicated and refuted.

FACT: the staging creates NO net-new control-plane or datastore write per unit of work.
The bind epoch is an in-process `int64` on `slotState` and `Server.bindEpoch`, never
persisted (spec-changes.md:688 "pod-local, and never persisted"); the reclaim hold is
`Server.reclaiming map[string]struct{}` guarded by `s.mu` (non-spec-changes.md:1003-1015).
No new informer, watch, CRD status write, Postgres row, or Redis key. The only added
per-failed-bind cost is one compensating `Shutdown` RPC. A grep of non-spec-changes.md
for postgres/redis/etcd/UpdateStatus/persist returns only pre-existing accounting prose.

FACT: the hold set is inserted and removed under `s.mu` but the destructive steps (drain,
`Runtime.Close`, `removeSlotTree`, scrub report) run OUTSIDE the lock — the hold survives
as a map entry, the mutex does not. EVIDENCE: non-spec-changes.md:1003-1010
(`reclaimSlotLocked` "runs the deregistration and ... inserts the identifier into the hold
set in the same critical section", `release` deferred by the caller). So there is no
pod-wide serialization of adapter RPCs behind a slot cleanup. I checked this specifically
because a naive reading of "reclaim hold" suggests a long-held lock; it is not one.

FACT: the §10.1.4 coordinator-lost hold termination is the longest-lived hold producer —
pass 1 (`deregisterStartedSessions`) takes a hold on EVERY started session at once and
pass 2 (`terminateHeldSession`) releases them serially under one shared 10s close context
(pkg/adapter/holdstate.go:190-205, :229-260; non-spec-changes.md:1009-1013, :2186-2188).
At `maxConcurrentSessions: 8` that is eight identifiers held for up to ten seconds.
I did NOT file this: the hold is keyed on slot identifier == session identifier, so it
blocks only a rebind of the same session, and in the SHIPPED tree that same window is
strictly worse — pass 1 already deregisters the entry, so a rebind onto the identifier
succeeds and pass 2's `removeSlotTree(m.state)`, which derives its paths from the slot
identifier, then deletes the fresh session's tree. The hold closes that latent bug. A
future filer needs a harm that survives this: the change makes this path more reliable,
not less.

FACT: the epoch's ABA-across-restart hazard is closed, and closed by the connection latch
rather than by the counter. `nextBindEpochLocked` seeds lazily from `time.Now().UnixNano()`
(non-spec-changes.md:997-1002), and spec-changes.md:688 states the epoch "survives neither
a pod restart nor a re-attach onto a replacement pod", while spec-changes.md:692 requires
the compensation to ride the connection its own attempt already holds and never re-dial.
A restarted adapter's connection is dead, so the stale epoch is never presented.

FACT: coordinator handoff degrades to the escape hatch rather than to a wrong teardown. A
successor replica holds no latched epoch on a connection it did not receive a response on
(spec-changes.md:692), so its `Shutdown` carries zero and is the unconditional teardown —
the shipped behaviour, unchanged. Nothing store-backed is relied on, so Postgres failover
and Redis reset do not change the epoch or the hold.

USEFUL [orchestrator brief]: the "already refuted" list is accurate and dense on this
lens — queue head-of-line serialization of the synchronous compensation, benign hold
refusals draining a pod at `maxConcurrentSessions: 2`, and the `slotCleanupBudget` floor
were each filed and refuted on materiality. Do not re-derive them; a new filing here needs
a harm none of those three arguments already absorbs.

### [non-spec-recheck-3.1.review-security.1]

DECISION: returned no findings — BECAUSE the whole delta for this firing is non-security:
`diff -ru` against the r3 snapshot shows edits only in `summary.md` (deletion of open decision
19, the 0080 impact row, plus two preamble sentences) and appended review-log blocks. No staged
spec text, no staged code, no test plan, no edit list changed. ALTERNATIVES: re-deriving the
epoch/hold security posture from scratch — rejected, seven prior sweeps plus this lane's earlier
security passes already covered it and the refuted list bars every close variant.

FACT: the reclaim hold cannot regress the §10.1.4 coordinator-lost teardown or the §11.4 revoke
fan-out, because pass 1 of the hold timeout ALREADY deregisters the entry before pass 2 destroys
it up to ten seconds later, in the shipped tree — EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/holdstate.go:190 (`members
:= s.deregisterStartedSessions()`), :200-205 (pass 2 under a 10s close context), :208-213 (the
doc comment states a later terminal `Shutdown` already skips its teardown because pass 1 removed
the entry). So a `Shutdown` arriving in that window answers `absent` today as well; CODE-6's hold
adds no new window in which a revoke is silently dropped.

FACT: the epoch is a liveness fence, not a security bound, and it fails in the safe direction.
An adapter that reports epoch 0 makes the gateway send the unconditional teardown; an adapter
that reports a mismatching epoch yields `SUPERSEDED`, which feeds the same adapter-self-reported
leak/clean-exit signal the shipped gateway already trusts (`err != nil || !cleanly`). The signal's
trust level is unchanged by this proposal, so there is no new pod-self-report bound under the
lens's check (2). The unfenced form remains the §11.4 revoke fan-out's, the recycle edge's and
`Binder.ReleaseSlot`'s — EVIDENCE: spec-changes.md:336-338; non-spec-changes.md:1077-1078
(`Shutdown` and `ShutdownRecycle` keep their signatures and pass a zero epoch).

WATCHOUT: the tempting security angle here is "a held slot identifier permanently denies binding
that session". It does not clear the bar: the hold set is keyed by slot identifier == session
identifier, its `release` is documented non-nil, idempotent and deferred on every return path
including panic (non-spec-changes.md:~995-1005), and the refusal is `codes.Aborted`, which both
gateway classifiers treat as transient. Do not re-file it.

### [non-spec-recheck.1.fix-G1]

CORRECTS [f2.open-decisions.out-of-scope-defects.slot-assigned-terminal]: its FACT "CODE-5 does not widen the unmodelled transition ... `BindReservedSlot` swallows its own reservation-release error" was true of the shipped tree and false of the staged tree. The same proposal's CODE-4 retires that swallow: its call-site table gives `BindReservedSlot` the value "`sbe.Leaked`, and the method sets `sbe.Leaked = true` on the error it is about to return when its own release fails" (non-spec-changes.md, the CODE-4 `ReleaseSlotReservation` call-site table), and CODE-5's reserved branch then passes that discriminator into `accountSlotFailure`, whose body is today's `MarkLeaked` plus leak gauge plus `RecordLeak` arm. A create-time-reserved connect-stage failure whose own reservation release errors therefore reaches `MarkLeaked` on a slot in `slot_assigned`. The summary row, the SPEC-4 exclusion paragraph, the spec-changes connect-stage edge-case bullet and the non-spec connect-stage edge-case bullet now say the staged lane adds one more producer of the transition, and the scope call rests on the surviving ground: the hole predates the proposal and is widened rather than created, the transition raises no runtime error because `Registry.Assign` and `Registry.Transition` have no production caller and `MarkLeaked` bypasses the edge list, and closing it means an edge out of `slot_assigned` that SPEC-4 deliberately does not add.

DECISION: the disposition stays `out-of-scope-stands` and SPEC-4 still adds the `receiving_uploads → slot_cleanup` edge alone. ALTERNATIVES: adding an edge out of `slot_assigned` was rejected because it cascades into CODE-3, DOCS-1, `TestValidTransitions_spec_6_2`'s exact edge set and §6.2's two-block concurrency scoping, and it half-closes (the same `MarkLeaked` call produces an equally unmodelled `receiving_uploads → leaked`); narrowing CODE-4 so `BindReservedSlot` reports `Leaked` false at the connect stage was rejected because the release runs with `leaked=false`, so a failed release means the Redis decrement did not happen and the slot really is leaked.

FACT: the tier-4 fixture cannot observe a pod retirement. `tests/tier4_integration/recycle_scrub_path_test.go` runs envtest with no WarmPoolController and asserts the `lenny.dev/drain-request` annotation directly, and both its concurrent pools carry `MaxConcurrentSessions: 4` (:807, :1016) against `UnhealthyThreshold = (maxConcurrent+1)/2` (pkg/gateway/runtime/slothealth/slothealth.go:215-220), so one leak reaches 1 of 2 and drains nothing.

FACT: `bound → recycling` is unreachable on the failed-bind release path with either disposition. `Binder.ReleaseSlotReservation` calls `claimer.ReleaseSlot(ctx, sandboxName, false, false)` with `recycle` hard-coded (pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:495-503) and CODE-4 adds only `leaked`; `SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot` reaches `WriteRecyclingStatus` only inside `if recycle {` (pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/slotclaimer.go:850). ### [spec.1.fix-bind-epoch]

In the surrounding specification "occupancy" is the pod's slot-counter occupancy (`spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:488`; spec-changes.md:548), so a third-party adapter author was told the epoch names the attempt that owns a pod-level quantity rather than the registry entry the epoch keys on. All four sites now read "owns a slot identifier": spec-changes.md:106 and :132 in the Design section, :630 in SPEC-5's §4.7.1 block, and :654 in SPEC-5's §15.4 bind-epoch contract. summary.md:44 restates the same sentence and is corrected with them.

The heading now reads "a retry skips the pod whose reclaim did not complete" and the index line "the retry after an incomplete reclaim carries `ExcludePods`". The narrative and test-case sites that describe an unacknowledged reclaim as one member of the class are unchanged, because each states a case rather than the rule.

SCHEMA-1's verification-set paragraph, which still read "the attempt's later bind-sequence requests", now reads "the later bind-sequence requests the session sends on that connection".

SPEC-5's closing rationale now states that both blocks put the epoch on the request side as well as the response side, that the wire edit landing them carries the field on each of the seven bind-sequence request messages, and that the mid-session upload rests on that field, because with every bind-sequence request epochless the first admission rule refuses one onto an identifier whose session has started. The spec text is unchanged: the two admission rules and the echo rule are the contract, and the wire staging owes the fields the DEFERRED line below enumerates. Exempting the §7.4 pair from the admission rules instead was considered and rejected: the exemption would oblige the adapter to tell a mid-session upload from a bind stage, which it cannot do on the wire (the pair is the same two RPCs), and §4.7.1 states it needs no way to.

### [spec-recheck.2.fix-slot-substate-fence]

These are corrections to the same pass that reworded the `running` boundary, appended here
because that pass left no subsection of its own in this file.

- **The reworded boundary contradicted "a start still in flight" inside its own paragraph.**
  The pass had set sentence 1 of SPEC-4's staged §6.2 prose to "dispatched to the pod's
  shared runtime process with its session identifier, which is the moment the
  `receiving_uploads → running` trigger above names", while the next clause still placed a
  start still in flight, dispatched and not yet arrived, in `receiving_uploads`. The two
  sentences named two different moments. The boundary is now stated once, at arrival: "A
  slot reaches `running` when the pod's shared runtime process has been given the session
  with its session identifier." The clause attributing that moment to the fence's trigger is
  deleted, so the paragraph states the boundary on its own authority and no longer glosses
  the trigger's words. The same substitution is applied to the Design section's parallel
  sentence.
- **The four parallel statements the pass did not reconcile now agree with the edited two.**
  Re-read after the edit: the §4.7 `Shutdown` row's "the slot's `running` sub-state and the
  cleanup-outcome report take the later moment, when the pod's shared runtime process has
  been given the session"; SPEC-3's withheld-report rule, keyed to "the sessions the pod's
  shared runtime process has been given"; SPEC-4's staged edge annotation, "before the
  runtime has been given the session, a start still in flight included"; and the edited
  paragraph's own later sentence, "a session the runtime has already been given is a slot in
  `running`". All four take arrival as the boundary, which is what sentence 1 now takes. The
  code and docs lanes already read arrival (`non-spec-changes.md:485` and `:1249`), so this
  edit falsified nothing there and that file was not opened.
- **What the edit deliberately does not do.** It does not touch the shipped

### [spec.3.fix-wellformedness-scope]

CORRECTIONS to the admission-cascade pass of spec loop round 3, from the post-fix review of
that pass's own edits. That pass left no shard in this file, so its corrections open one here
rather than a pass of their own.

- The pass restated the well-formedness rule with the literal criterion "a request on a message
  that carries `bind_attempt`", after deleting the classification that had bound the word
  "governed", and deleted "governed" from the restatement below it. §4.7.1 names the compensating
  `Shutdown` among the requests that carry `bind_attempt` (spec-changes.md, the "requests that
  carry `bind_attempt`" sentence), and a `Shutdown` asking for the unconditional teardown carries
  an empty token and no mid-session marker, so the rule as restated answered `INVALID_ARGUMENT` to
  every non-compensating `Shutdown` caller, contradicting the two-field rule in the same block and
  the §4.7 `Shutdown` row. Both sentences now scope the rule to a request other than a `Shutdown`
  and name the pairing rule that governs `Shutdown` instead, and §15.4's precedence sentence
  carries the same exclusion. The paragraph's "No rule is scoped by the name of an RPC" now opens
  with the `Shutdown` exception it had been disagreeing with three sentences later.
- The pass gave well-formedness a position relative to the cascade and none relative to the
  reclaim hold, the other pre-cascade check, so a request that is both malformed and names a held
  slot identifier had two conforming answers, one permanent and one transient. §4.7.1 now states
  the two checks in order: well-formedness first, because it is decided on the request's fields
  alone before the adapter reads the registry, then the hold applied to a well-formed request.
  §15.4's precedence sentence states the same order and its ground. This matches the staged code,
  where `validateBindFields` runs at the handler's entry before any resolve and the hold refusal
  is the first statement inside `ensureSlotStateLocked`.
- The `validateBindFields` bullet in the staged non-spec changes stated its exclusion as
  `StartSession` and `ConfigureWorkspace` carrying neither field, which does not account for
  `Shutdown`, whose message does carry `bind_attempt`. The bullet now names `Shutdown` and the
  rule that governs it, so the helper's scope is stated rather than inferred.

No staged deliverable is added, removed, merged, split or resequenced by these corrections, so
the implementation checklist gains no step and every box stays unticked. The summary needed no
edit: its CODE-6 index line names `validateBindFields` and its placement, both of which still
hold, and it states no scope for the well-formedness rule.

DEFERRED [implementation-checklist.md S13, the validator has no step that lands it]: the summary's
CODE-6 index line names "the `validateBindFields` check each handler that carries the fields runs
at its entry before the resolve" and the staged non-spec changes specify the helper, its predicate
and its call sites, while S13 is the only step for CODE-6 and enumerates that deliverable
exhaustively without naming the validator, its handler-entry placement, or the `INVALID_ARGUMENT`
refusal for the bind-sequence requests. S15's `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is `Shutdown`'s two-field rule
alone, and no other step covers it, so an implementor running the checklist as one sequence lands
§4.7.1's well-formedness rule nowhere and the tier-1 row that pins the gate has no step that builds
what it pins. The remedy is to extend S13 with `validateBindFields(bindAttempt, midSession)` in
`pkg/adapter/slot.go`, returning `codes.InvalidArgument` unwrapped when `(bindAttempt == "") !=
midSession`, called at the entry of `PrepareWorkspace` (on the resolving frame), `FinalizeWorkspace`,
`RunSetup`, `AssignCredentials` and `Resume` before any resolve, with the assertion that a refused
request leaves the registry and the on-disk tree unchanged. The checklist is outside this pass's
edit set.

### [spec.7.fix-pre-running-cleanup-actors]

CORRECTIONS to the pre-`running` cleanup pass of spec loop round 7, from the post-fix review of
that pass's own edits. That pass left no shard in this file, so its corrections open one here
rather than a pass of their own.

- The pass wrote the carve-out in SPEC-4's staged §6.2 paragraph and in SPEC-3's staged §5.2
  append with "a bind the §7.1 obligation does not reach" as its subject term, glossed in §6.2 as
  "a pre-attached bind on a pod serving one session". That set includes a `StartSession` that
  fails on a pod serving one session, which the same two sentences also place inside the
  adapter-handler arm, so each paragraph answered one case both ways. The tree settles it against
  the carve-out: `StartSession` claims the slot "whatever the pool's concurrency"
  (`pkg/adapter/session.go:108-111`) and every start-failure branch calls `releaseSessionSlot`
  (`pkg/adapter/session.go:133`, `:147`, `:157`), which deregisters the entry and removes the
  slot tree (`pkg/adapter/slotsession.go:214-220`) with no concurrency condition on the path. The
  subject term in both paragraphs, and in the Design rationale sentence that restates it, is now
  the binds the carve-out is true of: a bind that fails at the workspace-preparation, setup or
  credential-assignment stage on a pod serving one session, which neither the §7.1 obligation nor
  an adapter handler reclaims. A failed start on such a pod stays inside the adapter-handler arm
  the preceding clause states.
- The staged non-spec changes' accepted-failure-mode bullet on a cleanup that reports its failure
  nowhere still opened with the un-narrowed trigger, that any bind failing after
  `receiving_uploads` and before the runtime was given the session runs the cleanup in its
  failing handler. That is the statement the narrowing above withdrew, and the tree agrees with
  the narrowing: `releaseSessionSlot`'s production callers are start paths only
  (`pkg/adapter/session.go`, `pkg/adapter/resume.go`, `pkg/adapter/sdkwarm.go`), and no
  `PrepareWorkspace`, `FinalizeWorkspace`, `RunSetup` or `AssignCredentials` handler calls it.
  The bullet now names the three start handlers as the trigger and states separately that a
  failure at the workspace-preparation, setup or credential-assignment stage runs no adapter-side
  cleanup, so its residue is reclaimed by the §7.1 compensation or at the pod boundary.

No staged deliverable is added, removed, merged, split or resequenced by these corrections, so
the summary's deliverable index is unchanged and no statement in the problem statement or the
summary is falsified by them.

### [spec.8.fix-streaming-wellformedness-scope]

CORRECTIONS to the streaming well-formedness pass of spec loop round 8, from the post-fix review
of that pass's own edits. That pass left no shard in this file, so its corrections open one here
rather than a pass of their own.

- The pass qualified the well-formedness rule in the staged §4.7.1 streaming paragraph
  (spec-changes.md:773), stating that the rules are decided on the frame that resolves the slot
  identifier and that a later frame leaving either field at its default value repeats the call's
  assertion. It did not carry that qualification into the parallel §15.4 statement, which is the
  text a third-party adapter author implements against. §15.4's preamble and its well-formedness
  clause both stated the pairing per request, so an adapter written from §15.4 alone refused
  every §7.4 mid-session upload longer than one chunk: `mid_session` and `bind_attempt` are bare
  proto3 scalars with no presence (`schemas/lenny-adapter.proto:724`), and the sender builds each
  later frame from the session identifier, the upload reference and the chunk alone
  (`pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client.go:268-285`), so every later frame carries
  `mid_session` false with an empty `bind_attempt`. Both §15.4 sentences now say that on a
  `PrepareWorkspace` the two fields are read from the resolving frame and that a later frame
  leaving either at its default value is not evaluated against the pairing rule.
- CONF-1 clause (g) (non-spec-changes.md:1553) stated the same per-request pairing and would have
  built a conformance case refusing the handler CODE-6 stages, which calls `validateBindFields`
  on `PrepareWorkspace` only on the frame that resolves the slot identifier
  (non-spec-changes.md:1193-1194). The clause now names the resolving frame as the site the two
  fields are read from on that RPC.

No staged deliverable is added, removed, merged, split or resequenced by these corrections, so
the summary's deliverable index is unchanged, and no statement in the problem statement or the
summary is falsified by them.

  projects `claimed`, on a pool of either recycle setting" and added a rationale asserting that

  qualifying the opening clause to "a pod in a warm-inventory phase with no claim projects
  `idle`", and the rationale states why the no-claim clause is qualified with the other two.

  projection prose", and summary.md's SPEC-4 bullet records the no-claim clause's qualification

FACT: THE TWO LEAK LEDGERS SHARE ONE `slothealth.Tracker` INSTANCE, so the adapter-reported leak path and the gateway bind-failure leak path count into one threshold and cannot silently split a pod's leak budget. `cmd/lenny-gateway/sessiondeps.go:261` mints the single `slothealth.New(...)`, `wiring_fields.go:239` stores it, `main.go:254,265,323` hands the SAME pointer to both `sessionsrv.go:374 SlotHealth:` (the `applySlotRetryPolicy` / `accountSlotFailure` path) and `main.go:728-730 newScrubReportService(..., Tracker: slotHealth)` (the `drainLedger.RecordLeak` path behind `ScrubReporter.RecordSessionScrub`, pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegationtree/leasecontrol/scrubreport_server.go:468 and pkg/gateway/session/recycle/scrubreporter_seams.go:184-196). A future lens tempted to file "SPEC-3 withholds the `ReportSessionScrub` report so the leak lands in a different ledger than §6.2's trigger evaluates" should stop here: it lands in the same tracker, reached by a different caller. What genuinely differs is the GAUGE: `lenny_adapter_leaked_slots` is published only from the gateway bind-failure path (`slots.MarkLeaked` + `leakGauge`, start.go:2845-2848), never from the adapter-report path, and that asymmetry is pre-existing.

FACT: `SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot(ctx, name, recycle, leaked)` already implements the occupancy hold, so SPEC-3's and SPEC-2's "the slot is `leaked` … so it holds its occupancy" is discharged by CODE-4 threading `sbe.Leaked` into `ReleaseSlotReservation`. `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/slotclaimer.go:818,:830-831` skips the Redis counter decrement under `leaked`; `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:493-504` is the shipped `leaked=false` site the proposal parameterizes. An argument shaped "the gateway releases the reservation cleanly while calling the slot leaked, so the gauge and the Redis occupancy disagree" is false: `applySlotRetryPolicy` passes `sbe.Leaked` to the RELEASE and `sbe.Leaked || relErr != nil` only to the ACCOUNTING, so a pod-side-leaked slot is released with `leaked=true`.

FACT: the resume path's wire envelope claim checks out. `writePodClaimError`'s `default:` arm sets `Retry-After` and writes 503 with the caller's fallback code (pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:210-215), and `handleResume` passes `"RESUME_FAILED"` (start.go:3517), matching docs/reference/error-catalog.md:157. CODE-5's new `codes.Aborted` arm in `isTransientPodClaimError` (start.go:3648-3681) therefore aligns the row state with an envelope that already said retryable; it introduces no operator-visible state the docs do not already describe. spec/06:231-233 already routes BOTH retry-exhausted and non-retryable resume failures to `awaiting_client_action`, so the terminal-`failed` demotion the arm avoids is a pre-existing code-side behavior rather than something this proposal invents.

FACT: this round's snapshot delta is EMPTY for this lane. `diff -rq scratchpad/cp-snap/.../non-spec-recheck-3-r4 proposals/0081_...` reports only `...review-log.md` as differing; `non-spec-changes.md` and `summary.md` are byte-identical to the snapshot. DECISION: returned an empty findings list under the performance / scalability / failure-mode lens — BECAUSE nothing in the staging creates a net-new control-plane or data-plane write, a new watch, a hot key, or a store-backed dependency with no durable fallback, and the two capacity-tier angles my lens owns were already filed and refuted in earlier rounds (queue head-of-line occupancy during the compensation; benign hold refusal counted as a windowed slot failure at maxConcurrentSessions 2). ALTERNATIVES: I considered filing ExcludePods accumulation on a `queue` pool and the raised rate of `leaked` dispositions, and rejected both (see below).

FACT: the proposal adds NO persisted state and NO new RPC dial. The compensation reuses the connection the failed stage already holds (non-spec-changes.md:546-549), the bind epoch is an in-process `int64` on `Server`, and the reclaim hold is a `map[string]struct{}` on `Server` guarded by `s.mu` (non-spec-changes.md:994-1002). The only net-new etcd write is the existing `DrainSandbox` annotation stamp reached from two additional `accountSlotFailure` callers, and only at a threshold crossing. There is no informer, no watch, and no new connection pool.

FACT: the reclaim hold does NOT serialize the pod. `s.mu` is released before every destructive step in the shipped handler (pkg/adapter/session.go:234-239 unlocks before `drainViaLifecycle`/`Runtime.Close`/`removeSlotTree`) and CODE-1 preserves that ("No I/O runs under the lock on either", non-spec-changes.md:124-126). The hold is a map entry keyed on the slot identifier, and `SlotID == SessionID`, so it blocks only later attempts at the SAME session. Do not re-derive this as a lock-hold-across-`os.RemoveAll` bottleneck; it is not one.

FACT (verified arithmetic, so nobody re-runs it): `slotCleanupBudget = max(cleanupTimeoutSeconds / maxConcurrentSessions, 5)` seconds with Go integer division, and the graceful window sent on the `terminate` frame is half of it. The 5s floor puts the frame's `deadlineMs` at 2500ms or above on every pool configuration, against the schema minimum of 100. EVIDENCE: schemas/runtime-ops-events.schema.json:180 `"deadlineMs": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 100 }`; non-spec-changes.md:600-605.

WATCHOUT: `ExcludePods` accumulates across `waitInQueue` re-entries and nothing clears it (non-spec-changes.md:860-874). On a `queue` pool where every pod produces an unacknowledged reclaim, the list can grow to the whole pool, `ClaimSlot` then returns `ErrNoConcurrentSlot`, `isExhaustion` classifies it, and the request re-queues until `maxQueueWaitSeconds` and answers `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED`. I did NOT file this: the list is bounded by pool size, the terminal outcome is the specified exhaustion answer with `Retry-After`, the same pods are being drained by the health threshold anyway, and excluding them is exactly what §5.2's placement constraint states. A future filing here has to show a harm the bounded-queue timeout does not already absorb. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/queue.go:96-107, :185-214.

WATCHOUT: CODE-4 raises the RATE of the `leaked` disposition. Before this proposal `leaked` on the failed-bind path arose only when `ReleaseSlotReservation` errored; after it, it also arises on an unanswered or unclean compensating `Shutdown`, including a slot-tree removal that outruns the budget (non-spec-changes.md:540-545). Each leaked slot permanently withholds a Redis slot-counter decrement, so persistent-leak pressure toward the `ceil(maxConcurrentSessions/2)` replacement threshold goes up at concurrency 3 and above. I did NOT file this: it is the proposal's stated bounding mechanism ("the compensation's own failure is counted", summary.md, Decisions), the threshold itself is untouched, and the close variant was already filed and refuted. Anyone re-opening it must argue from a measured rate rather than from the mechanism.

A reviewer reasoning about "the successor's reservation being stolen" must first settle whether the successor took its own increment; on the create-time-reserved path it does not, because `bindConcurrentSlot` routes a row with a live `PodAssignment` to `BindReservedSlot`, which reserves nothing. DECISION: returned an empty findings list under the security lens — BECAUSE every security-shaped angle I derived is either (a) a strengthening, (b) pre-existing and explicitly recorded, or (c) already adjudicated. ALTERNATIVES considered and dropped, each with the ground that killed it:
- The bind epoch as an attacker-influenceable self-report. The adapter mints it and the gateway echoes it; a lying adapter could force `SUPERSEDED` and get `Leaked=false`. Dropped: the gateway already trusts `exited_cleanly` from the same component on the same RPC (`podsession/slotbinder.go` `leaked = err != nil || !cleanly`), and the adapter container is Lenny-managed while the untrusted runtime never sees this gRPC surface. No new trust boundary is crossed and no bound moves from a trusted measurer to a pod self-report.
- Loss of the "pod retires at occupancy zero" safety valve. `ReleaseSlotReservation` hard-codes `leaked=false` today, so a failed bind with no co-tenant DELETEs the claim and retires the residue-bearing pod; CODE-4/CODE-5 pass `sbe.Leaked`, and `SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot(leaked=true)` early-returns (no decrement, no DELETE), so the pod survives holding the leaked slot and stays a same-tenant placement candidate until §6.2's ceil(n/2) threshold. Dropped: the `leaked`-holds-occupancy disposition is already §6.2/§5.2 normative and already shipped on the ordinary release path; the proposal is applying it consistently, discloses it (summary.md:140 "pod retires through the shipped §5.2 threshold instead of accumulating residue", and the `maxConcurrentSessions >= 3` churn bullet at non-spec-changes.md:2081), and pods are tenant-pinned so no cross-tenant reach.
- CODE-1's narrowing of the runtime teardown from `bound` to `started`, against the §11.4 full-revoke fan-out. Dropped: §11.4 sends the unfenced zero-epoch form, and a bound-but-unstarted entry was never given to the shared runtime process, so nothing is skipped that a revoke needs; the same change WIDENS `removeSlotTree` from `bound` to `removed`, which newly reclaims `/run/lenny/slots/{sessionId}/credentials.json` for a registered-but-unbound entry.
- §15.4's mismatch non-conformance clause naming only three acts ("releases the slot, closes the runtime, or signals the shared runtime process") while CONF-1 asserts the workspace tree and credential file survive. Dropped: SPEC-3 widens §5.2's slot-release action list to include the credential directory and the armed §4.9 timers, so "releases the slot" subsumes the tree removal.

### [spec.1.fix-bind-attempt-token]

CORRECTIONS to the bind-attempt-token pass of spec loop round 1, from the post-fix review of
that pass's own edits. The pass left no shard of its own in this file, so its corrections open
this subsection rather than extending one.

- The SPEC-5 design commentary still stated the token/mid-session pairing as a universal ("The token field is non-empty exactly when the mid-session marker is false.", spec-changes.md), after the round narrowed that rule everywhere else. The staged §4.7.1 text scopes it to `PrepareWorkspace` and `FinalizeWorkspace`, has `RunSetup`, `AssignCredentials` and `Resume` always carry a non-empty token, and exempts `StartSession` and `ConfigureWorkspace` from the rule entirely; non-spec-changes.md and summary.md were scoped in the same round and this sentence was not. The commentary now states the same three cases in the commentary's own vocabulary, so the paragraph introducing SPEC-5 agrees with the block it introduces.
- SPEC-6's new `lenny_slot_compensation_outcome_unrecognized_total` row declared `pool` and `k8s_pod_name` labels that the site emitting the series cannot supply. The staged emitter is the default arm of CODE-4's `slotReclaimLeaked`, a free function with the signature `func slotReclaimLeaked(outcome adapterv1.SlotReclaimOutcome, cleanly bool, err error) bool` whose body is a bare `slotReclaimOutcomeUnrecognized.Inc()` (non-spec-changes.md), and the precedent CODE-9 cites is a `Binder` method taking exactly those two label values (`func (b *Binder) recordSlotFailure(errorType, pool, podName string)`, pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/slotbinder.go:358). §16.1 carries unlabelled counter rows already (`lenny_delegation_lease_extension_total`, `lenny_elicitation_timeout_total`, spec/16_observability.md), so the row now states the series as unlabelled and says why, and SPEC-6's lead-in distinguishes the superseded series, emitted from a caller holding the pool and the pod name, from the unrecognized-outcome series, emitted from the mapping that holds neither. The staged code is unchanged by this correction; the spec row was the defect.
- The envelope-residue bullet, written this round in both spec-changes.md and summary.md, mapped every setup-window refusal onto the non-retryable `SETUP_COMMAND_FAILED`. The shipped writer branches on the gRPC code rather than on the window: `writeSetupCommandError` answers 422 `SETUP_COMMAND_FAILED` only when `status.Code(setupFail.Cause) == codes.FailedPrecondition` and otherwise falls through to the 503 session-start fallback with `Retry-After` (pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:239-248). `SLOT_BIND_ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED` is answered on `ABORTED`, so a superseded `RunSetup` reaches the client on the retryable fallback. Both copies now split the setup window by code, and the bullet's conclusion on category and retryability, which the split leaves standing, is unchanged.
- The residues section's closing sentence in summary.md routed the recovery for every bullet in the list to position 2 of the remediation plan, after a fourth bullet was appended in the same round whose own text says narrowing the code is outside this proposal and which none of the three named position-2 mechanisms bears on. The sentence now names the three entry residues it covers and states separately that the envelope-naming residue has no position-2 work.
- The deliverable index's CODE-9 entry in summary.md still named the superseded series as "a compensation refused on a token mismatch", after the same file's fixed-decision bullet was rewritten in this pass to define it as a compensation answered `superseded`, meaning the adapter held an entry the compensation was not addressed to, so the reclaim released nothing. The staged definitions agree with the decision bullet: the §16.1 row states the same outcome (spec-changes.md) and the CODE-9 counter table states it with no expected rate (non-spec-changes.md). Under the caller-minted token there is no gateway series for a bind refused on a token mismatch; that refusal is the adapter's `ERROR_CODE_SLOT_BIND_ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED` answer on the bind RPC, which no staged counter observes. The index entry now names the same series, and its other two counters stand as they were.

The CODE-9 attribution paragraph in non-spec-changes.md asserted that both gateway counters take
a `SlotReclaim` hook on `Binder` "of the same form" as `recordSlotFailure`, which the unlabelled
§16.1 row falsifies for the unrecognized-outcome series. It is repaired in the same edit: the
superseded series keeps the hook, because its call site holds `req.Pool` and `sandboxName`, and
the unrecognized-outcome series takes no hook and no labels, because `slotReclaimLeaked` holds
neither value. No staged code, schema, chart, docs or test change was authored there.

No staged deliverable is added, removed, merged, split or resequenced by these corrections, so
the implementation checklist gains no step and every box stays unticked.
