It also let a later group discover that the design's line numbers had drifted and anchor on quoted strings instead of re-reading the file. Keep doing this.
- **Three RPCs admit a start, and §4.7's table carries all three.** `StartSession` (pod-warm, spec/04:672), `ConfigureWorkspace` (SDK-warm, :673) and `Resume` (:684) are all rows in the §4.7 Gateway→Adapter table, so the staged row's "which RPC in this table starts a session depends on the pod's session mode and on whether the session is new or resumed" resolves inside the table it names. spec/07:32-34 says SDK-warm pods skip `StartSession` outright, which is why naming that RPC in a predicate excludes every preConnect and resumed session.
- **The §7.3 re-attach claims from idle inventory.** `Binder.Resume` → `b.connect` → `podclaim.Claimer.Claim`, which takes only a Sandbox at `Status.Phase == Idle` (plus a same-tenant `reserved` rebind) and then CREATEs the deterministic per-pod claim; `ErrNoIdlePod` falls through to the §4.6.1 Postgres fallback, which re-reads the live Sandbox and refuses anything past idle. It never calls `ClaimSlot`. A pod holding a leaked slot keeps its `bound` claim, because `ReleaseSlot(leaked=true)` early-returns before `DeleteClaim`, so it is outside that candidate set with no `ExcludePod` needed. Nine lenses derived this independently; it closes the pass-1 OPEN "Resume path and the exclusion". EVIDENCE: podsession/binder.go:1590-1606,:1737-1768; podclaim/claimer.go:118-160.
- **That exclusion does not depend on Redis.** The reclaiming pod's per-pod `SandboxClaim` lives in etcd, so the §7.3 exclusion survives a Redis reset and the §12.4 rehydration hole does not reach it.
- **`ClaimSlot` pass 1 scans same-tenant CLAIMED pods with free capacity; pass 2 scans idle pods.** On the §5.2 bind path a leaked slot's held occupancy therefore filters nothing. Do not generalise the idle-inventory argument to the bind path. The UNVERIFIED that sat here, asking whether held occupancy makes the pod pass 1's own candidate, is RETIRED: it was a question about the placement exclusion, and no staged deliverable names that mechanism.
- **The three attempt kinds do not map onto three code paths, and `bindConcurrentSlot`'s reserved branch is a CONJUNCTION.** The guard is `if row.PodAssignment != "" && !session.IsRecovery(row.State)` (start.go:2595), so only a NON-RECOVERY row carrying a `PodAssignment` takes `BindReservedSlot` with no retry loop. A §7.3 resume-rebuild and a slotless row both reach `applySlotRetryPolicy` through `bindConcurrentSlot`, and so does a RECOVERY-state row (`resume_pending`, `resuming`, `awaiting_client_action`; pkg/api/v1/session/session.go:176-186) carrying a stale dead-pod `PodAssignment`, which falls through to :2606-2609 → `bindSlotWithRetry`. Each request builds a fresh `SlotBindRequest`, so `ExcludePods` never crosses a request boundary. CORRECTED (`non-spec-recheck-3.1.fix-G1.1`, FILED against summary.md:400 and fixed there): five earlier rounds wrote the unqualified "a row carrying a `PodAssignment` goes through `BindReservedSlot` and never enters `applySlotRetryPolicy`", citing the span `start.go:2594-2604`, which straddles the guard and the fallthrough. Cite `:2595` and `:2606-2609` separately. The conclusion those rounds drew is unchanged, because a recovery-state row is policy-placed and the staged placement exclusion covers it.
- **`applySlotRetryPolicy` wraps `binder.BindSlot` only,** and branches on `*podsession.SlotBindError`, so it governs BIND failures rather than only adapter-reported failures of a running slot. `BindReservedSlot` (start.go:2596) and `ClaimSlot` (:2148) are called directly and never traverse it. `maxSlotRetries == 1` bounds one invocation to two attempts, but a `queue` pool re-enters the whole closure with the budget starting over (queue.go:143-146,:205), so a single-valued exclusion field is NOT sufficient: a second unacknowledged reclaim on a second pod would replace the first name. CODE-5 stages `ExcludePods []string` and appends. CORRECTED (`spec.1.review-performance.1`): the re-entry fires ONLY on an exhaustion sentinel. `runWithQueue`/`waitInQueue` abort on any other error and the whole wait is deadline-bounded (queue.go:134-147,:193-212), so a transient `ABORTED` reclaim-hold refusal cannot restart the budget and there is no livelock inside one request. The slice is still the right design, because a second exhaustion genuinely does re-enter.
- **`BindReservedSlot` re-runs the whole `materializeSlot` sequence** (stage → finalize → setup → credentials → `StartSession`) against the persisted `row.PodAssignment` and `row.ID`, so a retried §15.1 start reaches the same pod, the same slot id and the same on-disk tree. Its failure keeps the row `ready` and returns a retryable `STARTING_FAILED` with a `Retry-After`, and nothing in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver` clears `PodAssignment`.
- **A create-time-reserved slot exists only on a concurrent pool.** `bindConcurrentSlot` is the sole caller of `BindReservedSlot` and is reachable only under `match.MaxConcurrentSessions > 1`; the exclusive create-time binding goes through `Binder.Launch`'s reconnect instead.
- **The slot routes are concurrency-gated end to end.** Every one sits behind `match.MaxConcurrentSessions > 1` (start.go:2139, :2351, :2465), and the exclusive path goes through `failPhase`, which drains the pod. So `ReleaseSlot(leaked=true)`'s early return can never falsify §7.1's "the pod retires" sentence, and §7.1's exclusive branch is grounded in the pool setting rather than in momentary occupancy.
- **`Launch`'s reconnect failure returns the pod to the pool rather than draining it,** through `ReclaimClaimed` (binder.go:977-991), but that failure precedes the attempt's first session RPC, so §7.1 owes no reclaim there. `ReclaimClaimed` sends no `Shutdown` at all: it deletes the per-pod claim and revokes the §4.9 lease, leaving the adapter's slot entry untouched on a concurrent pod.
- **`SlotClaimer.ReleaseSlot`'s `recycle` parameter, not `leaked`, patches the claim `bound → recycling`,** arms the missing-report timeout and returns `recycled`. `ReleaseSlotReservation` passes `recycle=false`, so a failed bind that drives occupancy to zero DELETEs the claim and the pod retires rather than recycling. That bounds the pass-1 "recycle boundary on a failed bind" question.
- **`Binder.Resume`'s failure branch releases nothing on an exclusive pool.** `reserveResumeSlot` returns `""` when `MaxConcurrentSessions <= 1` and `releaseResumeSlot` no-ops on an empty slot id; `resumeOnPod` returns the error with no rollback, and `holdOrFailOnResumeError` touches only the session row. A failed §7.3 re-attach therefore leaves the replacement pod `claimed` until §4.6.1 orphan GC.
- **§7.2 owns the mid-resume close sequence.** "Mid-resume terminal transitions — snapshot-close semantics" (spec/07:210-216) is the five-step sequence BOTH §6.2 `resuming` bullets defer to, and its step 3 carried the premise this proposal overturns ("no runtime was started on it, so no scrub beyond the pool's default post-session scrub is required"). SPEC-2 stages three §7.2 edits.
- **§7.2's sequence is only partly implemented.** Steps 4 and 5 exist (`bumpCoordinationGenerationOnSnapshotClose`, `recordSessionCompleted`); steps 1 and 3 have no implementation on the DELETE path. Correcting step 3's text therefore creates no code obligation and needs no code deliverable.
- **Neither §6.2 `resuming` bullet enumerates §7.2's sequence.** Both omit step 4's `coordination_generation` bump, which is why the sibling bullet's "abort / skip-seal / release-replacement-pod / run-terminal-handling" gloss is a pointer rather than a list that must grow, and why the `resuming → completed` bullet needs no edit when the reclaim joins the sequence.
- **The mid-resume reclaim rides the aborted attempt's own still-open connection,** under a detached context, before `cl.Close()` and the release. That is why it belongs at step 3 rather than step 1, and it is what makes "sends on the connection that attempt still holds" implementable.
- **§6.2's pod fence retires a failed pod.** `claimed ──→ draining (terminal claim disposition released or failed)`, `failed ──→ draining`, `draining ──→ terminated`, with no `failed → idle` edge, and spec/05:455 says a session that ends in failure always retires its pod. The prose at spec/06:283 ("marked `failed` and released back to the pool") is the loose statement and the fence governs.
- **A `leaked` slot cannot wedge a pod's retirement.** `draining ──→ terminated` is triggered by "pod replacement provisioned from warm pool" and is not gated on occupancy reaching zero, so occupancy held forever delays nothing. §4.6.1 orphan GC drains such a claim rather than returning the pod to idle.
- **DECISION: §7.1's obligation window ends when the attempt SUCCEEDS,** rather than when it "has the session running on the pod". `running` is bound vocabulary pinned by SPEC-4, so the old clause ended the obligation exactly where the next sentence says it must not.
- **DECISION: §7.1 states no cleanup-outcome report rule at all.** Its closing sentence was deleted outright rather than scoped. The report rule, its pre-`running` exception, its complement and the one-report-per-release rule are all SPEC-3's, appended to §5.2's `**Scrub model.**` paragraph, which the other sections cite.
- **DECISION, SUPERSEDED at round 11 and replaced in place: the cleanup-outcome reporting rule is a BICONDITIONAL in §5.2's `**Scrub model.**` OPENING SENTENCE.** The superseded form was "SPEC-3's §5.2 append states the complement", as a second sentence lower in the same paragraph reading "A cleanup that reclaims a slot the pod's shared runtime process was given is a session release like any other and reports its outcome." Its CONTENT was right (the positive half must be stated rather than implied) and its LOCATION was wrong: the paragraph's own opening sentence (spec/05:453) still asserted the universal "a per-slot cleanup runs on every session release, reported by the adapter via `ReportSessionScrub`", so one rule had two statements and the stronger one was the one the tree has never satisfied. SPEC-3 now REPLACES that opening sentence with a biconditional — the adapter files `ReportSessionScrub` when, and only when, the cleanup is one a `Shutdown` performs to reclaim a slot the pod's shared runtime process was given — and DELETES the complement. The biconditional covers the SDK demotion, the §10.1.4 hold-timeout termination and the failed-start rollback without naming any of them. ALTERNATIVES rejected: enumerating the exempt paths beside the complement (a third statement of one rule, and the enumeration was already incomplete, because `releaseSessionSlot`'s failed-start rollback is a third non-reporting release); deleting the complement and leaving :453 alone (leaves the false universal as the spec's only statement); adding the report to the demotion and hold-timeout paths in code (double-counts one session against `recycle.maxSessionsPerPod`). EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/session.go:279 is the tree's one `reportSessionScrub` caller; pkg/adapter/sdkwarm.go:296-301, pkg/adapter/holdstate.go:219-220 and pkg/adapter/slotsession.go:214-220 are the three that reclaim and file nothing.
- **DECISION: the SPEC-3 range is one canonical phrase,** "abandoned or fails after its slot enters `receiving_uploads` and before it reaches `running`", written identically into the staged §5.2 append, the Design rationale, and summary.md's What-changes bullet and SPEC-3 deliverable-index line. SPEC-4 adds an edge only out of `receiving_uploads`, and the `slot_assigned` case is deliberately left open.
- **DECISION: §7.2 takes three edits.** The preamble's premise sentence is deleted whole and the reason for skipping the live seal moves into step 2, which owns the decision; step 2 gains one sentence saying the aborted re-attach's pod-side state is reclaimed in step 3 rather than sealed; step 3 is replaced.
- **DECISION: the create-time-reserved retry bullet is keyed on acknowledgement.** The "bounded on both sides" claim was deleted and both arms re-keyed on whether the adapter acknowledged the reclaim, because the adapter's refusal is `st.started` while the gateway's `leaked` is `err != nil || !cleanly`, which made the old second arm exactly backwards and the old first arm false for every pre-start stage. The bullet's charter is to RECORD a residue no layer governs, and a record needs no bound.
- **DECISION: SPEC-1 stages a third block, on spec/29.** One sentence appended to §29.4 session-end step 13 restates the graceful-shutdown signal's co-tenancy condition and cites §4.7, and `spec/29_communication-scenarios.md` joins "Spec files touched". §29.4 step 12 is left unedited.
- **The drain gate and the runtime close have different preconditions in shipped code.** `Shutdown` sends the CH-RUNTIMEOPS drain only under `if !boundRemains`, then closes the runtime unconditionally for a bound entry. No `spec/` text stated the drain gate before this proposal: it lives at docs/reference/adapter-contract.md:75 and in code, which is why applying SPEC-1 creates a new spec-internal contradiction rather than exposing an old one.
- **`terminate` is the only §29 site that emits the graceful-shutdown signal.** §29.7 (drain) and §29.9 (eviction) carry checkpoint frames, so SPEC-1's single §29 site is the complete §29 mirror for the new condition.
- **The `terminate` frame carries `type`, `deadlineMs` and `reason` and no session field,** on the per-pod abstract socket `@lenny-runtime-ops`, so "the signal is pod-global and names no session" is accurate. The Basic/Standard stdin `shutdown` frame is also pod-global (§28.5.3's CH-MSGSOCK card excludes `heartbeat` and `shutdown` from the session-addressed set), so the claim holds at every integration level.
- **`ShutdownRequest.reason` is a plain `string` with no enumeration,** so the code lane's `"slot_bind_failed"` mints no wire value and needs no proto or SDK edit. The closed four-value enum belongs to the intra-pod `terminate` frame only, and `drainReason` normalises anything unrecognised to `session_complete`.
- **§29's preamble subordinates a trace on DISAGREEMENT and says nothing about omission.** So §29.2's silence on the finalize-block failure branch and §29.6 step 4's `RESUME_FAILED` branch are omissions rather than edit sites. It is also not a licence to leave a trace stale: this proposal edited step 13 rather than relying on the resolution rule, so an argument that "§29 is only a restatement" has to explain why step 13 was edited and a sibling was not.
- **§29.2's atomicity restatement covers its own steps 2-10,** which end at the `session_id` return, and the first pod-side RPC in that trace is step 15 `PrepareWorkspace`. So the widened §7.1 parenthetical quantifies over an empty set there and spec/29:200 stays accurate unedited.
- **`spec/16_observability.md` needs no edit and can orphan no alert.** There is no metric or alert row for leaked slots, per-slot cleanup or session scrub; the rows that touch the surface (`lenny_gateway_pod_retirement_total` :12, `lenny_slot_failure_total` :14, `lenny_slot_pod_replacement_total` :15, `lenny_pod_session_reuse_count` :128) all stay true, and `WarmPoolExhausted` keys on the `lenny_warmpool_idle_pods` gauge rather than on the client-visible error code.
- **`ReportSessionScrub` has no missing-report timeout,** unlike `ReportPodScrub`, so a withheld report trips no gateway-side watchdog and produces no spurious retire. It is also emitted once with no retry, so the at-most-one invariant is not defeated by redelivery even though `RecordSessionScrub` has no dedup key.
- **`slotlayout.EnsureTree` creates five directories per slot and `RemoveTree` removes four trees** (slot root, `/sessions/{id}`, `/artifacts/{id}`, `CredentialsDir`). §6.4 names three of them and defers removal to §5.2; neither §5.2's whole-pod scrub steps 1-6 nor step 0 sweeps `/sessions/` or `/artifacts/`, so the per-slot cleanup is the only spec'd reclaim for them.
- **SPEC-3's two added actions are shipped and correctly qualified.** `RemoveTree` sweeps `p.CredentialsDir` and `deregisterSlotLocked` cancels every armed provider timer before deleting the entry. §4.9's timer is direct-delivery-mode only (spec/04:1169), so the qualifier is exact and the clause is vacuous rather than wrong in proxy mode. §5.2:455 and scrub step 0 already presuppose the wider list, so the widening is a catch-up rather than a new obligation.
- **§4.7.9 step 5 is `PrepareWorkspace → FinalizeWorkspace → RunSetup → AssignCredentials → StartSession`.** The connect stage sits outside it: `connectSlot` does only `resolveSandbox`, `DialAdapter` and `NegotiateVersion`, which is pod-scoped and creates no adapter entry. So "a bind abandoned at the connect stage owes no reclaim" is sound, and the narrowed SPEC-3 range and §7.1's "first pod-side RPC" name the same boundary.
- **On the create-time-reserved path every stage that can fail before `StartSession` is pre-start,** so `st.started` is false for each and `claimSessionSlotUnderLock` admits the retry. The adapter refuses a repeat start on `st.started` alone, never on entry presence and never on the binding.
- **`Shutdown`'s entry removal and its tree removal are two moments.** `deregisterSlotLocked` runs under `s.mu`; `removeSlotTree` runs afterwards outside the lock, synchronously inside the handler before the response is built. Because `compensateFailedSlotBind` blocks on `cl.Shutdown`, an ACKNOWLEDGED reclaim has finished its tree removal by the time the gateway returns the error to the client.
- **The `Shutdown` handler performs no context-expiry check,** so a reclaim whose gateway-side deadline has already lapsed still executes destructively when it reaches the handler: it removes the entry, cancels the timers, closes the runtime for a started entry and removes the tree.
- **The leak disposition is keyed on the gateway's acknowledgement,** `leaked = err != nil || !cleanly`, rather than on what the adapter did with the entry, so an entry the adapter removed and acknowledged is released. `applySlotRetryPolicy` sets `ExcludePod` under `sbe.Leaked || relErr != nil`, a third arm no spec sentence names.
- **`SocketRuntimeProcess.Start` has no acknowledgement step.** It adds the session to the active set and returns, and it returns nil immediately when `p.connected` with no ctx check, so a racing `StartSession` on a cancelled context still starts the session. That is what makes both orderings of the reclaim-versus-claim race reachable rather than theoretical, and it is why "whose session the runtime has not yet acknowledged" names a handshake the platform does not have.
- **`ensureSlotStateLocked` calls `slotlayout.EnsureTree` BEFORE registering `s.slots[slotID]`,** and `EnsureTree` has no rollback, so a mid-way failure leaves directories on disk with no registry entry, which the staged §4.7 no-op rule then certifies as clean. Judged inert: the directories are empty and `MkdirAll` is idempotent on the retry.
- **A retry inherits the slot TREE and nothing else.** `assignCredentialsSlot` rewrites `st.creds` and the on-disk credential file wholesale from the request's lease set, `reconcileSlotExpiryTimersLocked` cancels timers for absent providers and re-arms the rest keyed on lease id, and `onSlotLeaseExpired` re-reads the slot state and returns unless the captured lease id still matches.
- **The retried start runs on occupancy the counter no longer counts.** `BindReservedSlot` releases the create-time reservation on failure through `ReleaseSlotReservation` → `ReleaseSlot(..., false, false)`, a real `active_slots` decrement, while the retry reconnects to the persisted binding and re-reserves nothing. Pre-existing and outside this proposal.
- **The reclaim's deadline is bounded.** The code lane wraps `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` in `slotCleanupBudget`, a `WithTimeout` of `max(cleanupTimeoutSeconds / maxConcurrentSessions, 5)` with a 5s floor, and SPEC-1 plus SPEC-3 carry §5.2's formula across the concurrency boundary. §7.1's "states no deadline" reads as unbounded only in isolation.
- **The CRD cleanup-timeout rule is concurrency-gated in code.** `poolstore.validateSessionPolicy` puts the `cleanupTimeoutSeconds >= maxConcurrentSessions*5` check inside `if sp.MaxConcurrentSessions > 1`, so any spec sentence generalising that bullet across the concurrency boundary generalises an admission rule the code does not apply at concurrency 1.
- **The occupancy-zero concurrent release sends TWO RPCs.** `Binder.ReleaseSlot` sends the per-slot `Shutdown`, then a second `ShutdownRecycle` reusing the just-released session id over the same connection; the exclusive release sends one `ShutdownRecycle` for a session the adapter does hold. That asymmetry is why SPEC-1's no-op sentence reads differently on the two paths.

SPEC-2's §7.1 sentence restates an existing §5.2 definition. A fourth kind would be an unowned-residue finding, and there is none.

- **DECISION: the compensating `Shutdown` splits its two bounds by SHRINKING the adapter's grace.** `compensateFailedSlotBind` hoists `budget := slotCleanupBudget(req.CleanupTimeoutSeconds, req.MaxConcurrentSessions)`, uses it for the `context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), budget)`, and passes `budget/2` as `cl.Shutdown`'s fourth argument. `slotCleanupBudget` keeps its signature. ALTERNATIVES rejected: doubling the RPC bound to twice the §5.2 figure (the most faithful reading of §5.2, whose figure is the adapter's enforcement number, but it doubles a worst case that already degenerates to the whole 60s `cleanupTimeoutSeconds` on an exclusive pool reached through `Binder.Resume`, inside a path holding the client's HTTP request); a named `slotCleanupGrace` helper or a package constant (one relation belongs in one place, and a bare constant is a non-spec default with no override); `slotCleanupBudget` returning `(budget, grace)` (equivalent and acceptable, but take it INSTEAD of the inline `budget/2`, never both); leaving `deadlineMs` at zero and widening the RPC bound alone (impossible, because with zero the adapter derives its grace FROM the RPC context's deadline).
- **With `deadlineMs: 0` the adapter's SIGTERM pivot and the gateway's give-up instant are the SAME instant.** `contextWithGraceDeadline(ctx, 0)` returns the inbound RPC context unchanged (session.go:327-332), and `resolveShutdownGrace` PREFERS that context's remaining deadline over the runtime-configured grace and over the package default (mcpruntime.go:311-324). A runtime that uses its grace was therefore ALWAYS reported unacknowledged, so a completed reclaim was recorded `Leaked`. That is the defect the split closes.
- **The strongest production-reachable argument for the split is the `terminate` frame, not the runtime close.** `Shutdown` feeds `req.GetDeadlineMs()` into `drainViaLifecycle` (session.go:260), `RuntimeOps.Terminate` serialises `DeadlineMs int32` with `omitempty`, and the frame REQUIRES `deadlineMs` with `minimum: 100`. `budget/2` is at least 2500ms because the budget carries a five-second floor, so this call site becomes schema-correct as a side effect. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/runtimeops.go:65,:486-490; schemas/runtime-ops-events.schema.json:180-183.

- **DECISION: "slot-identifier occupancy" is renamed the **slot-identifier reclaim hold** and re-windowed.** It starts in the critical section that deregisters the entry, ends when the cleanup finishes, and carries no `leaked` clause. - **DECISION: §7.1 carries ONE leak predicate, "did not complete".** A reclaim did not complete when the adapter did not answer it, or answered `reclaimed` without reporting a clean exit; `superseded` and `absent` are completed reclaims and leave the slot unleaked. §5.2's `**Max retries:**` bullet and its commentary read "did not complete" / "incomplete reclaim" to match. That is exactly CODE-4's discriminator and SPEC-3's §5.2 clause, so spec, staged clause and shipped mapping are one statement.
- **DECISION: §7.1's retry-exclusion rationale is the reclaim hold rather than tree reuse.** The adapter admits no bind onto a held identifier, so a further attempt cannot reuse a tree the reclaim is deleting; it is refused transiently. CORRECTED (`spec.6.fix-G1.1`): the clause that charged such a refusal to the §5.2 retry budget is RETIRED, because the exclusion is exactly what stops a policy-placed retry ever reaching the hold. §7.1 and the Design now read "an attempt that meets the hold is one the retry policy did not place". §5.2's `**Max retries:**` bullet carries no reason of its own, so §7.1 is the only place the exclusion is motivated. CORRECTED AGAIN (`non-spec.2.fix-G1.1`, filed by `non-spec.2.review-reliability.2`): the exclusion reaches only a hold the RECLAIM opened. After CODE-6 routes `releaseSessionSlot` through `reclaimSlotLocked`, the abandoned attempt's OWN pre-`Runtime.Start` rollback opens a hold as well, and the gateway can see nothing that distinguishes it: the compensating `Shutdown` is exempt from the hold, finds no entry and answers `ABSENT`, which CODE-4 correctly reads as a completed reclaim, so the pod is not excluded and a policy-placed retry meets the live hold and spends its last attempt (`maxSlotRetries` is 1). The exclusion is therefore unwidenable without new wire surface and the residue is accepted. The three staged sites that stated the universal were FIXED by `non-spec.2.fix-reclaim-hold-callers`; see the Settled entry on those three sites for what they now say and for the UNVERIFIED beside it.

- **§5.2's CRD webhook makes the 5s floor unreachable on an admissible concurrent pool.** It rejects any pool with `cleanupTimeoutSeconds < maxConcurrentSessions × 5`, so `slotCleanupBudget` is always `cleanupTimeoutSeconds / maxConcurrentSessions` and at least 5s, and larger on a generous pool. The proposal's repeated "an unset pool yields the 5s floor" framing understates the typical budget; at the spec's own canonical pool (`cleanupTimeoutSeconds: 60`) it is 15s at concurrency 4.
- **The per-pool claim FIFO is strictly head-of-line serialized.** Only the ticket at the head re-enters `attempt(ctx)`, and the next waiter is admitted by `yield` or `dequeue`, both of which run after `attempt` returns, so latency added inside a bind attempt is multiplied across every queued request for that pool. EVIDENCE: start.go:2606; queue.go:191,:205,:220,:240-280. This is a different mechanism from the refuted "`ExcludePods` head-of-line-blocks the pool FIFO" dress, which was about a waiter that yields to the tail.

- **DESIGN GENERATION: the bind epoch is withdrawn and the mechanism is a gateway-minted per-attempt BIND ATTEMPT TOKEN.** The 2026-09-16 hand revision (commit e53e4800a) replaced it wholesale. The gateway mints one token per bind attempt from a cryptographically secure source (16 bytes hex in the code lane), the adapter stamps it on the entry it creates, compares it for equality and never mints one of its own, and no response reports a token. Every entry below that argues in epoch vocabulary is a record of the withdrawn design.
- **The token-carrying request set is five, and it is closed.** `PrepareWorkspace`, `FinalizeWorkspace`, `RunSetup`, `AssignCredentials` and `Resume` carry `bind_attempt`; `PrepareWorkspace` and `FinalizeWorkspace` are the two that also carry `mid_session`. `StartSession` and `ConfigureWorkspace` carry NEITHER field and are governed by the started-session rule alone. Every other RPC resolves an entry the session already holds, creates none, and is outside the admission rules.
- **`mid_session` already ships on `FinalizeWorkspaceRequest` (field 4) and does NOT exist on `PrepareWorkspaceRequest`,** whose field 4 is `reserved "slot_id"`. SCHEMA-1 adds the marker to `PrepareWorkspace` only, which is why §15.4's wire sentence names one message while §4.7.1 names two. More than a dozen shards have read this backwards off a single grep hit. EVIDENCE: schemas/lenny-adapter.proto:713-724, :682-696.
- **The SCHEMA-1 field numbers under the token design, verified free by many independent lenses.** `PrepareWorkspaceRequest` `bind_attempt`=5, `mid_session`=6 (1-3 used, 4 reserved); `FinalizeWorkspaceRequest` `bind_attempt`=6 (1-4 used, 5 reserved); `RunSetupRequest` 5 (4 reserved); `AssignCredentialsRequest` 4 (3 reserved); `ResumeRequest` 16 (6 and 15 reserved); `ShutdownRequest` `bind_attempt`=7 and `unconditional_teardown`=8 (1,2,3,5,6 used, 4 reserved); `ShutdownResponse` `slot_reclaim`=3. Do not re-derive these, and do not carry the retired nine-number epoch table forward.

- **Two adapter `ErrorCode` values are minted, 28 and 29, and they take NO §15.1 row.** `SLOT_BIND_ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED` is answered on `ABORTED` with `CATEGORY_TRANSIENT`; `SLOT_BIND_ALREADY_STARTED` on `FAILED_PRECONDITION` with `CATEGORY_PERMANENT`. The precedent is `ERROR_CODE_PROTOCOL_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE = 27` (schemas/lenny-adapter.proto:585), which is published through §15.4.2 alone (spec/15:1699) and has no §15.1 catalog row. `spec/` carries no adapter-ErrorCode catalog anywhere.
- **§15.1's catalog is the CLIENT-facing `code` table with an HTTP Status column** (spec/15:1002,:1006). A row there asserts the code reaches a client. The gateway renders no adapter `ErrorCode` into a REST envelope on any staged path, so a row for either new code would be a category error. That is the ground on which the staged §15.1 sub-block and the first DOCS-3 were deleted.
- **The `Shutdown` selector is two fields and the request must ask for exactly one.** A request carrying a `bind_attempt`, and a request carrying `unconditional_teardown`, are the two legal forms; a request carrying neither, and a request carrying both, is answered `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Every non-bind caller (the §11.4 revoke fan-out, the occupancy-zero recycle edge, `Binder.ReleaseSlot`, `Binder.shutdownAdapter`) must set the flag, which is a code-lane obligation worth a test.
- **The admission cascade has a published ORDER, and it is: the §5.2 reclaim hold, then field well-formedness, then the rules for a request that resolves no entry, then the attempt-identity rule, then the started-session rule.** The hold and the well-formedness check both PRECEDE the cascade rather than sit inside it. The staged code evaluates in exactly that order, and §15.4 says explicitly that its clause set is not an evaluation order and points at §4.7.1 for the one that is.
- **A request meeting both the differing-token condition and the started-entry condition is refused `SLOT_BIND_ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED`,** so a stale bind identity stays transient rather than becoming the permanent `SLOT_BIND_ALREADY_STARTED`. The overlap is reachable and the two codes carry opposite client retryability, so the tie-break is load-bearing.
- **Field well-formedness is `validateBindFields(bindAttempt string, midSession bool) error` in `pkg/adapter/slot.go`,** returning `codes.InvalidArgument` when `(bindAttempt == "") != midSession`, unwrapped, called at the entry of the five handlers whose messages carry the fields. It does NOT route through `slotResolveError`, which would re-present it as a slot-resolve failure and hand `SlotBindError.Reason()` a workspace-validation reason.
- **`StartSession` and `ConfigureWorkspace` both CREATE the entry when none exists,** through `claimSessionSlot` → `claimSessionSlotUnderLock` → `ensureSlotStateLocked`, so either can mint an UNTOKENED entry. That entry is answered `superseded` by a named reclaim (fail-closed, because it may be a live successor's), is released only by the unconditional teardown or by the pod's retirement, and refuses every later bind attempt at that session on that pod. It is a recorded accepted residue with recovery routed to position 2 of the remediation plan. EVIDENCE: pkg/adapter/session.go:111; sdkwarm.go:217; slotsession.go:75.
- **`FinalizeWorkspace` is UNCONDITIONAL on both bind paths and precedes the start,** so on any correct ordering the entry is always created by a token-carrying RPC and the untokened entry needs an abandoned or late start to occur. `PrepareWorkspace` is the conditional one (uploads only). EVIDENCE: podsession/binder.go:921; slotbinder.go:291.
- **`SLOT_BIND_ALREADY_STARTED` on `RunSetup` is reachable, by the interleaving §4.7.1 itself describes.** Attempt B's `PrepareWorkspace` creates the entry under B's token; abandoned attempt A's late `StartSession` carries no token, is admitted because the entry has not started, and starts the session on B's entry; B's `RunSetup` then matches on token and falls to the phase gate. Do not dismiss the setup-window envelope mapping as unreachable.

Every `RunSetup` error is wrapped in `*SetupCommandFailure` on both bind paths, and `writePodClaimError` checks the typed setup case first. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go:186-194,:217-249; podsession/binder.go:933-943; slotbinder.go:299-305.

- **DECISION: the `ExcludePod(s)` placement mechanism is WITHDRAWN WHOLE, and no placement rule survives anywhere in the staging.** `grep ExcludePod` over the staging returns nothing outside the review logs. What governs a retry meeting the reclaiming pod is the per-attempt token compare (a surviving entry) or the reclaim hold (a running cleanup), and both refusals are transient. §5.2's `**Max retries:**` bullet is left exactly as it stands.
- **§5.2's retry placement prefers the SAME pod.** "The retry is always assigned to a **new slot** on the same pod (if a slot is available) or on a different pod from the pool (if the original pod is fully saturated or unhealthy)" (spec/05:555). `applySlotRetryPolicy` re-submits the identical `req` with no exclusion and `maxSlotRetries == 1`, so a same-pod refusal is the request's last attempt.
- **`WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` is the claim-exhaustion code and is NOT §5.2's retry-budget exhaustion.** It is reached only through the `ErrNoConcurrentSlot`/`ErrNoIdlePod`/`ErrTenantMismatch` sentinels the retry loop returns unchanged; the budget exhaustion returns the structured `error.category` error of the `**Client error on exhaustion:**` bullet. Do not write `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` into any retry-budget narrative.
- **DECISION: §7.1's reclaim obligation is scoped by whether the pod survives the failure, rather than by a list of call sites.** It binds the §15.1 start transition onto a slot on a pod serving concurrent sessions (reserved at creation or placed by §5.2's retry policy) and the §7.3 re-attach onto a replacement pod. `Binder.Prepare` and `Binder.Launch` drain the pod through `failPhase` and send no compensation at all, so the exclusive start discharges the obligation by retirement.
- **DECISION: SPEC-2's §7.1 atomicity-parenthetical edit is DELETED and the shipped parenthetical stands.** Session creation leaves no pod-side state to reclaim on either pool class: on an exclusive pool `Binder.Prepare`'s failure closure drains the pod, and on a concurrent pool `prepareAtFinalize` returns before any adapter RPC. SPEC-2's §7.1 block is now one inserted paragraph and no in-place edit.
- **The finalize gate is one line and it is the warrant for "no adapter RPC runs at finalize on a concurrent pool".** `finalize.go` returns `(nil, nil)` before `s.podBinder.Prepare` when `match.ExecutionMode == service || match.MaxConcurrentSessions > 1`. §7.1's own numbered flow reads as if steps 11-13 do pod I/O at finalize, and §15.1:646-647 carries the carve-out ("On a concurrent-workspace pool whose reserved slot materializes and runs setup at start"). Several lenses have lost a pass trying to falsify this.
- **`Binder.Prepare` runs at `/finalize` and `Binder.Launch` at `/start`, two independent HTTP requests, with nothing carrying in-process state between them.** `Launch` re-dials and issues only `ConfigureWorkspace` or `StartSession`. That is why neither can hold `Prepare`'s token, and it is the load-bearing reason the two starts carry none.
- **DECISION: the reclaim hold's bound is stated by chaining through §5.2's own `**Slot cleanup:**` bullet.** The two sentences arguing that the bullet's timeout is "not a second bound" and that the directory removal runs "under no deadline" are deleted. The hold lasts as long as the cleanup; on a pod serving concurrent sessions a cleanup that overruns the bullet's timeout is a failed cleanup, so the slot is `leaked` and its identifier stays held until the pod terminates. Ending the hold at the timeout was rejected as actively unsafe: releasing the identifier while `os.RemoveAll` runs readmits a successor onto a tree being deleted. CORRECTED in round 14: the identifier-hold half of this decision is RETIRED. SPEC-3's staged §5.2 text no longer carries the "so the slot is `leaked` and its identifier stays held until the pod terminates" clause; the hold's bound is the cleanup's return on every arm, success or failure, and the disposition of a cleanup that does not complete is the scrub-model paragraph's `leaked` clause alone, which §7.1 reads off the response's clean-exit answer. The identifier hold and the `leaked` occupancy are separate objects. The rejection of ending the hold at the timeout stands as written. CORRECTED AGAIN and SUPERSEDED in round 3 of the spec recheck (`spec-recheck-2.3.fix-G3.1` and `fix-design-G3.1`): the round-14 retirement of the identifier-hold half is WRONG, because `leaked` is a gateway-side accounting state read off the `Shutdown` response's clean-exit answer, fences nothing on the pod, and no adapter surface refuses admission on it, so after the retirement the failed-cleanup arm had no fence at all. The live rule is in the Settled entry on the completion-keyed hold: the hold ends when the cleanup COMPLETED, meaning every act it owed the slot returned without error, and where the cleanup does not complete the identifier stays held for the life of the pod. The `f1` firing's deletion of open decision 12 rested on the same retired reasoning and is superseded with it.

- **RESOLVED: a pod serving one session has TWO exits, and SPEC-4's §6.2 paragraph is the single
home that states both.** The retiring exit is the one every failed bind takes: the release reaches
occupancy zero, the per-pod claim is deleted, and the occupancy projection drains a `claimed` pod
whose claim is gone rather than returning it to inventory. The return-to-pool exit is `reserved →
idle`, reached through the recycling binding state once the adapter's whole-pod scrub has been
reported, on either production path that writes `reserved` and on a failed scrub as well as a
successful one, because the default `onScrubFailure: warn` returns a failed-scrub pod to the pool
with a `scrub_warning` annotation. The scrub removes every per-slot workspace tree and credential
file the pod still holds and verifies their absence from disk, independently of the adapter's
registry; the registry entry and the armed lease-expiry timers are not reached by it. §7.1's staged
paragraph, SPEC-3's §5.2 append and the accepted-failure bullet each cite that paragraph and restate
nothing, and the `slot_cleanup → released` sole-exit half is answered by it too: on the pod class
that offers no `leaked` sub-state, a cleanup that runs completes and releases, and a bind neither
actor reclaims drives no edge at all. EVIDENCE: pkg/controller/warmpool/occupancy.go:126-140;

- **DECISION: the `PrepareWorkspace` per-frame predicate is asymmetric and is stated as one default-value principle.** Neither `bind_attempt` nor `mid_session` carries presence on the wire, so a later frame leaving either at its proto3 default asserts nothing and repeats the resolving frame's assertion; only a non-empty `bind_attempt` differing from the resolving frame's, or `mid_session` true where the resolving frame's was false, is a disagreement. ALTERNATIVES rejected: dropping the per-frame comparison (loses the fail-closed refusal and leaves clause (i) unpinnable); obliging the sender to restate both fields per frame (the adapter cannot tell a repeated `false` from an omitted one, and §15.4 is published to third parties); giving `mid_session` explicit presence (new wire surface, and it splits the two forms of one field).
- **DECISION: the admission rules, well-formedness included, are decided on the RESOLVING frame's values.** Stated in the same paragraph as the per-frame principle, because applying the well-formedness pair per frame refuses every later frame of a mid-session upload before the disagreement rule is reached.
- **`sendUpload` sends no per-frame marker at all.** Each `PrepareWorkspaceRequest` frame is built from `SessionId`, `UploadRef` and `Chunk` alone, chunked at 64 KiB (`prepareWorkspaceChunkSize`), and one `PrepareWorkspace` call loops over the whole uploads map, so the resolving frame is the first frame of the first upload and every frame of every later upload is a later frame. EVIDENCE: pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client.go:240,:247-265,:269-284.

There is NO crash-takeover and no coordinator-handoff `Shutdown`; `pkg/gateway/coordination/` contains no `Shutdown` string, and the re-adopt sends `CoordinatorFence` alone. CODE-4 sets `unconditional_teardown` in the builder, so no caller edit is owed. Derived independently by at least eight shards; do not re-derive.
- **There are TWO recycle-carrying `Shutdown` senders and they reach DIFFERENT arms.** The concurrent path (`Binder.ReleaseSlot`) sends a plain unconditional `Shutdown` at slotbinder.go:542 and then `ShutdownRecycle` at :574, so the second finds no entry and answers `absent`. The session-mode path (`Binder.Release`'s recycle branch, binder.go:1974 → :1994 → `shutdownAdapter(..., true)` → :2037) sends the recycle request as the session's ONLY teardown, so the entry is live and the outcome is `reclaimed` on the removing arm. That path is production-live: `exclusiveBindRequest` sets `Recycle: match.Recycle` (start.go:2520,:2561), so any exclusive pool with recycling reaches it on every non-failed release.
- **`startPodScrub` is asynchronous.** It spawns a goroutine and returns (podscrub.go:40-42), so firing clause three from the removing arm blocks nothing under the slot guard or the reclaim hold. It does run CONCURRENTLY with the per-slot cleanup those two protect, which no staged text orders.
- **DECISION: CODE-1's handler has ONE exit, `answerShutdown(outcome, exitedCleanly, untokened)`,** which counts the untokened row, runs clause three (`if rc := req.GetRecycle(); rc != nil { s.startPodScrub(rc) }`) and builds the response; the shipped trailing clause three at session.go:283-291 is DELETED in the same edit, or the scrub runs twice and `ReportPodScrub` double-sends. Two returns deliberately bypass the helper because they perform nothing: the two-field precondition's `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and the shipped empty-session-id check at session.go:228-230.
- **DECISION: the per-slot guard's scope is a PREDICATE plus a derivation table, never an RPC enumeration.** A section that does path work against the slot's tree outside `s.mu` acquires that slot's guard before the resolve that hands out its paths and holds it until that path work ends; a section whose path work runs inside `s.mu` takes none. The predicate selects `PrepareWorkspace`, `FinalizeWorkspace`, `RunSetup` and `Resume` on the admission side and the three destructive sections on the other. EVIDENCE for the exemptions: `assignCredentialsSlot` writes the credential file inside its own `s.mu` section (slotcreds.go:24-44); `ConfigureWorkspace`'s only write is `writeSessionManifest` under `Server.ManifestDir` (manifest.go:280-283, server.go:111-114), which `slotlayout.RemoveTree` does not touch (tree.go:58-69).
- **`Server.Resume` is the adapter's largest UNLOCKED path write,** which is why the enumeration that omitted it was wrong. `checkpointRootsForSession` copies the roots under `s.mu` and RELEASES it (slot.go:183-207); `restoreChunks` then fetches every chunk over the network and runs `workspace.ExtractTree` with no lock (resume.go:169-208, called at :106).
- **DECISION: the guard is `map[string]chan struct{}` (capacity-one semaphores) and both hand-out forms are context-bounded.** `lockSlotGuard(ctx, slotID) (func(), bool)` and `acquireSlotGuardForResolve(ctx, slotID) (func(), error)` both select the send against `ctx.Done()`. The expiry disposition is NOT uniform: a destructive section that cannot acquire proceeds unguarded and logs `slot_guard_not_acquired` (which is today's shipped behaviour, so no regression); an admission RPC that cannot acquire is refused with `ctx.Err()`, because proceeding unguarded is how a materialization re-creates a tree the reclaim just removed.
- **DECISION: `Shutdown` compares under `s.mu` FIRST, acquires the guard only on the arm that destroys, and RE-DECIDES under `s.mu` afterwards.** Every arm that removes nothing answers from the fast path and never waits, because the guard's holders are unbounded in wall time (`workspace.MaterializeWithPolicy`/`MaterializeOverlayWithPolicy` take no ctx at all, materialize.go:157,:203; `RunSetup` runs under a `setupPolicy.timeoutSeconds` spec/14:99 permits to be absent) while the reclaim's budget is `max(cleanupTimeoutSeconds / maxConcurrentSessions, 5)`s and a timed-out reclaim is charged a permanent leak. The re-decision is sound against every remover: the only writer that can remove an entry without taking the guard is §10.1.4 pass 1, which removes under `s.mu` alone, and the re-decision catches exactly that and answers `absent`.
- **The guard STRICTLY CONTAINS the reclaim hold on a single-pass reclaim.** `defer unlockSlot()` is registered before `defer release()` and Go runs defers LIFO, so `release()` runs first. Consequence: a guarded workspace RPC racing a reclaim BLOCKS rather than being refused, and the hold's refusal survives only for the unguarded entry-creating RPCs and, on the §10.1.4 two-pass path, in the window between `deregisterStartedSessions` (hold, no guard) and `terminateHeldSession` (guard). That is why the hold is tested at BOTH `acquireSlotGuardForResolve` and `ensureSlotStateLocked`: they are one predicate at two points, not two mechanisms.
- **DECISION: §10.1.4's ten-second budget is RE-SCOPED rather than divided.** `onHoldTimeout`'s single `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)` becomes the pass's GUARD-ACQUISITION deadline alone, and `terminateHeldSession` mints its own ten-second close context after the acquisition returns, which `emitFinalUsage` and `Runtime.Close` run on. BECAUSE the shipped pass is a serial loop over pass 1's whole member set sharing one context (holdstate.go:196-205,:237,:249), so any wait charged to it is charged to every LATER member. SPEC-3's staged §5.2 sentence already bounds "the cleanup's close" per cleanup, so this is a mis-scoping correction rather than a new rule. ALTERNATIVES rejected: a per-member slice of the shared budget (invents arithmetic and still burns member 1's own grace); deleting the guard from `terminateHeldSession` (needs an exception to the guard predicate and re-opens the `ExtractTree`-versus-`removeSlotTree` race); one per-member context covering both acquisition and close (a parked holder still burns member 1's close grace).
- **DECISION: `releaseSessionSlot` splits into a guard-acquiring form and `releaseSessionSlotUnderGuard`,** because `Resume` holds the slot's non-re-entrant guard across its whole call and its seven rollback sites (resume.go:69,:73,:89,:107,:126,:134,:141) would otherwise self-deadlock on every `Resume` failure, which no happy-path test reaches. It also gains a `context.Context` first parameter; every production caller has a handler ctx in scope. Production callers: session.go:133,:147,:157 and sdkwarm.go:236,:241,:251,:298. `Server.ReleaseSlotForTest` (export_test.go:32-35) gains the ctx too and has five callers (integrationlevel_test.go:84, credexpiry_test.go:320, checkpoint_stream_test.go:1012, tracingcontext_addressing_test.go:425, one_session_only_test.go:77).
- **`releaseSessionSlot` calls NO `Runtime.Close`.** Its whole body is `deregisterSlot` → `removeSlotTree` → `cancelPodMCPIfRuntimeIdle` (slotsession.go:214-220). Only `Shutdown` and `terminateHeldSession` (holdstate.go:251-252) close a runtime on a cleanup path.

- **DECISION: CODE-8 is a closure SIGNATURE change, `reclaim := func(cause error)`, plus an enumerated call-site sweep.** Both reclaim closures are `func()` with no parameters and no returns (binder.go:866-869, :997-1000), and every call site declares its failing error in its own `if`/`else if`, so a guard written into the bodies does not compile in `Prepare` and silently never fires in `Launch`.
